input.summary: Edit a plate reference and see it applied to the print specimen.
limits: References contain two uppercase letters, a hyphen and two digits; invalid values are identified after blur.
checks: Edit and blur invalid/valid references; verify the specimen, associated error, helper count and focus.
guidelines: Keep the real RAMS primitive, label and helper/error association; motion decorates the same control rather than replacing its anatomy.

textarea.summary: Edit the edition colophon with a matching preview and remaining-character help.
limits: The native limit is 140 characters. Blur checks for at least eight characters after trimming leading and trailing spaces.
checks: Edit, clear and recover the colophon; verify the real preview, count, associated error and native limit.
guidelines: Keep the real RAMS primitive, label and helper/error association; motion decorates the same control rather than replacing its anatomy.

select.summary: Choose the cover stock and update the actual paper weight and finish.
limits: Three cover stocks have fixed weights and finishes. Only one stock is selected.
checks: Choose each stock by keyboard; verify selected text, weight, finish and trigger focus.
guidelines: Keep the real RAMS primitive, label and helper/error association; motion decorates the same control rather than replacing its anatomy.

switch.summary: Toggle crop marks on the actual plate using the same RAMS switch anatomy.
limits: The function is binary. Only the thumb response differs from the base switch; the model owns the crop marks.
checks: Toggle by pointer and keyboard; inspect marks, label, thumb boundaries, resize and reduced motion.
guidelines: Keep the real RAMS primitive, label and helper/error association; motion decorates the same control rather than replacing its anatomy.

password-field.summary: Edit and reveal the proof passphrase while preserving the native field value.
limits: Reveal changes the input type and its pressed action; the character count follows the current value.
checks: Edit, reveal and hide; verify value/selection, action name, pressed state and focus.
guidelines: Keep the real RAMS primitive, label and helper/error association; motion decorates the same control rather than replacing its anatomy.

accordion.summary: Read one production answer at a time while the panel follows its content.
limits: Three production notes use single, collapsible selection; the first note starts open.
checks: Open, collapse and traverse questions by keyboard; verify only the selected answer is exposed and live reduced motion settles it.
guidelines: Compose the owned RAMS primitive; preserve its anatomy, semantics and current information while motion follows the selected state.

tabs.summary: Compare stock, ink and imposition studies with a moving selection and measured panel changes.
limits: Three production studies select one panel. Overflowing tab strips scroll locally; a focused tab is revealed.
checks: Traverse tabs by keyboard, check the matching artwork and panel, local strip bounds, resize and live reduced motion.
guidelines: Compose the owned RAMS primitive; preserve its anatomy, semantics and current information while motion follows the selected state.

alert.summary: Add or remove actual trim marks and read the matching warning or success message.
limits: Adding or removing marks changes the four corners of the displayed plate and the matching readiness state.
checks: Add and remove marks; verify title, tone, icon, complete action and matching artwork through motion/reduced motion and reflow.
guidelines: Compose the owned RAMS primitive; preserve its anatomy, semantics and current information while motion follows the selected state.

progress.summary: Check the actual stock, ink and fold tasks and see the matching fraction and percent.
limits: Three checklist states derive one native progress value with max 3; toggling a task reverses the same model.
checks: Complete and undo checks; compare native value/max, counted percent, fill, keyboard and reduced motion.
guidelines: Keep value and max in the same units; derive percent and fill from that ratio.

skeleton.summary: Replace a labelled placeholder with the original cover specimen, then show the placeholder again.
limits: The Reveal cover action controls local placeholder/content presence; no timed transfer is claimed.
checks: Reveal, reset and repeat; verify busy/status visibility, complete artwork, focus and live reduced motion.
guidelines: Keep the placeholder labelled, hide decoration, and replace it with the actual content.

badge.summary: Mark the ink proof checked or reopen it while its status label and tone update in place.
limits: The model owns one binary proof state; the label always identifies the state.
checks: Mark and reopen by pointer/keyboard; verify badge text, action wrapping, focus, resize and reduced motion.
guidelines: Use text to state the proof status; motion and color add emphasis without replacing the label.

empty-state.summary: Add the first cover to the rack, inspect the actual artwork, and remove it to recover the empty state.
limits: The empty state is shown only while there is no cover; actions update one local cover.
checks: Add and remove by keyboard; verify actual cover, empty recovery, new action focus, labels and reflow.
guidelines: Use an empty state only while the rack has no cover; actions update the displayed content.

avatar.summary: Cycle through named workshop stations with original marks and matching assignments.
limits: Five station marks and assignments share one selected index; these are original resource identities, not portraits.
checks: Cycle all stations; verify matching mark, visible and accessible name, assignment and retained button focus.
guidelines: Identify the resource by its name as well as artwork; changing station updates both.

avatar-sizes.summary: Compare the same station mark at four honestly labelled circular diameters.
limits: This optical geometry specimen uses fixed diameters of 28, 36, 48 and 88 px while explanatory text stays fluid.
checks: Measure all four actual circles and inspect labels, image loading and reflow.
guidelines: Preserve circular geometry; labels show the actual CSS-pixel diameter.

avatar-presence.summary: Change the station availability between online, offline and not shown.
limits: The local availability state updates the indicator, text and accessible name together.
checks: Cycle the three states by keyboard; verify indicators, accessible names, text and focus.
guidelines: Expose availability in the name and text, including when no status is shown.

avatar-initials.summary: Use station initials without artwork, then load their original marks without changing identity.
limits: Three resources keep their names as artwork is added or removed.
checks: Verify initials, load/recover/remove marks, accessible names and unchanged action focus.
guidelines: Show the correct mark once it loads; keep the resource name unchanged.

avatar-group.summary: Expand three visible station marks into the full five-station collection and assignment list.
limits: The same five stations supply both the overlapping group and complete assignment list.
checks: Expand and collapse; verify three/five visible marks, remaining count two/zero, full assignments, action state, focus and reflow.
guidelines: Name the collection, expose remaining count and allow opening a complete assignment list.

radio-group.previewTitle: Fold-pattern selection with a measured highlight
radio-group.summary: Choose the same paper fold while a single measured highlight follows the selected row.
limits: The motion wrapper retains its existing controlled label/options/value/onValueChange/name API.
Primitive-only form, disabled, orientation and loop configuration are not added to the motion wrapper.
checks: Use labels, Arrow keys and Space; verify native input checked state and focus, including a short press.
Home and End move focus without changing selection; Space selects the focused option.
Verify uncontrolled and controlled form reset, native required validation and external form association in the clean consumer.
Change selection, enable reduced motion mid-spring and compare the highlight with the already selected row.
Resize text/viewport, inspect focus-visible rows and verify cleanup after unmount.
guidelines: Keep one geometry owner for the row highlight.
Descriptions name the actual choice; visual movement does not commit the selection.
Use the primitive directly when a consuming form needs its wider native configuration.

button.summary: Switch between a cover and its four-page print imposition while the action label and width change.
limits: The fold view changes local artwork; it does not create a print file.
checks: Activate with Enter and Space; retain focus as the label changes.
Switch reduced motion during the label morph and resize to a narrow viewport.
guidelines: Use one primary action for the active composition.
Keep changing labels specific to the next operation; disabled Reset fold becomes available only in the unfolded view.

action-button.summary: Validate an edition name and calculate a SHA-256 fingerprint from the actual local drawing parameters.
limits: Web Crypto must be available in a secure browser context.
This fingerprint identifies the sample name and drawing parameters; it is not a prepress inspection, colour proof, or authenticity certificate.
The native pending state follows the operation; no artificial delay is added.
checks: Submit an empty edition, read the error, then enter a name and retry.
Compare the displayed digest with the SHA-256 of the documented JSON bytes.
Check pending reentry, focus retention, caller refs and unmount during an unsettled operation in a consuming fixture.
guidelines: Use pendingLabel and successLabel for the actual operation.
Handle rejected work with onActionError and provide a visible recovery route.
Keep focus on the action while it is pending; animation never gates the digest result.

split-button.summary: Download original one-colour poster artwork in portrait or square proportions through a main action and its menu.
limits: Exports SVG files generated in this browser; it does not submit a print order.
The downloadable artwork uses system sans-serif text and contains no private font files.
Browser download behaviour remains user-agent controlled.
checks: Download the current format and verify the filename and non-empty SVG contents.
Open the alternatives by keyboard, download the other format and verify focus returns to the trigger.
Repeat with reduced motion and a narrow viewport; the trigger must remain a stable anchor.
guidelines: Keep the main action frequent and alternatives closely related.
Menu selection must perform the named export and update the artwork proportion.
Treat the joined surface as one action composition and keep other view actions secondary.

button-group.summary: Navigate three original wayfinding artworks with joined actions and a sheet chooser.
limits: The group changes local artwork only; sheet choice is not persisted.
Each segment is a button or a native link; the group does not assign a selected/tab role.
checks: Check both disabled endpoints and the corresponding artwork.
Use ArrowLeft/ArrowRight, Home/End and Tab; then select a sheet in the menu.
Check compact-label collapse and recovery after increasing available width.
guidelines: Use a group name that identifies the shared object.
Disabled individual actions remain discoverable through aria-disabled while suppressing activation.
Reserve labels when a consumer needs stable segment width across known label changes.

floating-button-group.summary: Toggle an alignment grid, registration marks and mirroring on an original two-ink composition.
limits: The controls modify the local SVG; they do not edit an external design document.
No keyboard shortcuts are advertised or bound by this scenario.
checks: Toggle every tool and compare pressed state with visible artwork.
Use the toolbar arrow keys and Home/End; confirm a single roving tab stop.
Focus icon-only tools and inspect their own RAMS tooltip; check live reduced motion during highlight travel.
guidelines: Use aria-pressed for tools with persistent on/off state.
Keep the floating tray adjacent to the artwork it affects.
The tray owns its shared moving highlight; its native buttons retain a visible focus outline.

expanding-button-group.summary: Rotate, mirror, invert and reset a local block-print matrix while labels expand on focus or hover.
limits: The drawing changes immediately; confirmation labels are temporary feedback.
The component exposes one busy and confirmation indicator; consumers must coordinate overlapping asynchronous actions.
On touch, an action whose label is collapsed needs a reveal tap before activation.
checks: Use Rotate, Mirror and Invert, then reset and compare the matrix.
Use keyboard arrows and Home/End, including disabled Reset at the initial state.
Test reveal-then-activate on touch and live reduced motion while width changes.
In a consuming async fixture, reject an operation and confirm no doneLabel is announced.
guidelines: Use short verb labels and factual doneLabel text.
Keep the result available immediately and keep disabled actions labelled.
Use onSelect=false or a rejection when confirmation should be suppressed.

text-reveal.summary: Presents a short printmaking sentence as a heading with its mount-time entrance.
limits: The entrance runs at mount; the final heading remains available without animation.
checks: Reload the preview to observe the entrance
Confirm the heading remains readable
guidelines: Use a concise factual sentence
Keep the heading semantics intact

in-view-title.summary: Lets the reader select among word, line, blur, tracking, and wipe entrances for a registration heading.
limits: Changing the selected style remounts this heading to replay its entrance.
checks: Select every entrance style with the keyboard
Check that the heading is readable in each style
guidelines: Keep the heading short enough to read
Treat the selector as a local presentation control

text-morph.summary: Changes a visible proof label between Ink proof and Paper proof.
limits: Only the proof label changes; its button stays mounted and keyboard-focusable.
checks: Activate the button repeatedly
Confirm the current label and button action stay in sync
guidelines: Use brief, distinct labels
Name the action for the next value

text-shimmer.summary: Shows a print-registration sample label with a control for pausing or resuming its visual sweep.
limits: The status reports the enabled setting; reduced motion can keep an enabled label still.
checks: Pause and resume the sweep
Confirm the status text matches the control state
guidelines: Use a meaningful static label
Keep the pause control explicit

code-block.summary: Displays a short local CSS layout example with the component's copy and expand controls.
limits: The initial view shows five lines; Copy code includes the complete CSS source.
checks: Use the copy control
Expand and collapse the displayed code
guidelines: Keep the snippet self-contained
Set its filename and language to match the content

expandable-text.summary: Shows original print-workshop notes that can be expanded and collapsed.
limits: The collapsed note keeps three lines; the toggle is omitted when the content fits.
checks: Read the note in both collapsed and expanded states
Check wrapping at a narrow width
guidelines: Preserve the complete note when collapsed
Use enough real content to demonstrate truncation

copy-button.summary: Copy the visible Rosario edition reference to the actual clipboard.
limits: Clipboard access requires a supported secure context and permission; failures remain actionable.
checks: Copy with the keyboard; verify the complete reference in the clipboard and retain focus.
guidelines: Show the exact value being copied and name its action.

checkbox.summary: Add or remove registration marks from the print sheet.
limits: The artwork retains its position while the marks change.
checks: Toggle the checkbox and confirm the marks appear and disappear
Check that its visible label activates the control
guidelines: Use a checkbox for an independent on/off choice.

segmented-control.summary: The segmented control switches the displayed sheet between its front, reverse, and plate detail views.
limits: Front, reverse and detail are views of the same sheet.
checks: Select each view and confirm its title, description, and illustration change together
Use arrow keys or Home and End to move between options
guidelines: Make each segment select a real view of the same subject
Keep the selected view named in the content

rating.summary: A five-level rating records an impression-alignment score for the illustrated proof and shows the current value.
limits: Five named levels describe contour alignment. Click the selected star again or press Delete or Backspace to clear the score.
checks: Choose several values and confirm the visible score changes
Clear the rating and confirm the status returns to Not rated
guidelines: Name each rating level clearly
Keep the displayed result in sync with the control

slider.summary: Adjust an original river print’s margin in millimetres and inspect the resulting printable rectangle.
limits: The output is calculated from the current control value.
checks: Press Home on Margin. 6 mm margin; printable rectangle 198 × 136 mm.
Start at 12 and press ArrowRight. 13 mm margin; printable rectangle 184 × 122 mm.
Press End, then try moving beyond the maximum. 24 mm margin; printable rectangle 162 × 100 mm; value remains bounded.
Drag and release the thumb, including a release near a bound. The output and SVG describe the actual stepped value emitted by the slider.
At 320px and root 200%, inspect all controls, derived outputs and artwork without clipping or font reduction; repeat keyboard focus and live reduced-motion checks.
guidelines: Use an explicit unit in format and the derived output.
Keep the original sheet size visible so the margin calculation has context.
Use a short control label and a flowing result when the derived dimensions need more space than a header readout.

number-field.summary: Set the number of ink passes, add the corresponding SVG separation layers, and calculate impressions for sixty sheets.
limits: Impressions are arithmetic for this sample edition; no press job is submitted.
During an invalid or incomplete draft, the artwork retains the last accepted value until the component commits a valid value.
Label scrubbing, decimal affixes and locale variation are not enabled in this specimen.
checks: Activate Increase Passes once from the initial value. 4 input value, 4 SVG ink-layer groups and 240 impressions.
Set 1, then try decreasing again. 1 layer and 60 impressions; decrease remains focusable with the component’s existing limit feedback.
Press End in the spinbutton. 8 layers and 480 impressions; increase indicates its upper limit.
Type 0 or an incomplete draft and commit with Enter or blur. The existing NumberField draft/limit rules apply; artwork follows only accepted values and recovery remains possible.
At 320px and root 200%, inspect all controls, derived outputs and artwork without clipping or font reduction; repeat keyboard focus and live reduced-motion checks.
guidelines: Keep the accepted value distinct from an incomplete input draft.
Expose the edition quantity next to the resulting impression count.
Use the existing width custom property for a responsive composition; do not shrink the numeric text or step targets.

elastic-slider.summary: Adjust the overlap of two one-hundred-millimetre panels and inspect their combined width.
limits: This is a geometric joint study; it does not certify a physical overlap, press tolerance or ink result.
The component engine owns elastic stretch, release momentum and detents; verify reduced-motion behavior in the consuming layout.
checks: Press Home on Overlap. 0 mm overlap; two panels meet at the edge; combined width 200 mm.
Start at 12 and press ArrowRight. 13 mm overlap and 187 mm combined width.
Press End. 24 mm overlap, right panel x=96 in diagram units and combined width 176 mm.
Drag through the numeric marks and release. The geometry follows the actual stepped/detent value; stretch does not change the output beyond 0–24 mm.
At 320px and root 200%, inspect all controls, derived outputs and artwork without clipping or font reduction; repeat keyboard focus and live reduced-motion checks.
guidelines: Distinguish visual elastic travel from the bounded value used for geometry.
Keep both source panel widths visible when displaying the derived width.
Use numeric detents without long absolute-positioned tick labels when the surrounding composition must accommodate enlarged text.

icon-morph.summary: Use button-sized icon transitions to show changes of action or state.
limits: These controls change local presentation; they do not send alerts or alter external settings.
checks: Toggle all eight icons by pointer and keyboard, including reversing a transition.
Inspect icon drawing and alignment in both states at desktop and narrow widths.
Change reduced motion during a transition and verify the latest state.
guidelines: Pair a changing icon with a stable accessible name and the appropriate pressed state.
Use the actual icon at control size; surrounding artwork must not replace the demonstrated interaction.
demonstrates: Toggle eight independent icon buttons between their actual two states.
Keep accessible button names and pressed state while the icon changes.

json-viewer.summary: Edit a Tucumán edition and inspect its calculated sheet records, copy totals and impression count in the JSON tree.
limits: Title edits apply immediately, including an empty title.
Sheet records are paged four at a time; search highlights matching keys and values and opens their branches.
Copy actions are omitted with copyable=false.
checks: Edit Edition title; the title value in the tree follows the input.
Folio with 24, 48 and 72 copies produces 12, 24 and 36 sheets, with 24, 48 and 72 impressions respectively.
Cards with 24, 48 and 72 copies produces 6, 12 and 18 sheets and the same respective impression counts.
Open sheets and load the next page; the row quantities sum to the selected copy count.
Search for Rain, impressions and a missing term; clear the query and recover ordinary tree navigation.
Use the tree's arrows, Home, End and Enter; the wrapping Selected path output follows the active row.
Inspect the tree and external controls at 320px/root 200%, in both themes and with reduced motion.
guidelines: Calculate totals and per-sheet rows from the same configuration values.
Keep editable fields separate from tree navigation.
Use a flowing path output when a selected path needs to remain readable at enlarged text sizes.

slot-text.summary: Select a signed horizontal correction for a Rosario registration detail and read its numeric two-decimal reel value.
limits: The sample offers four corrections: −1.25, 0.00, +0.50 and +1.50 mm.
The millimetre unit is outside the reels; the diagram is a magnified registration detail.
checks: Initial value is the number -1.25; its formatted text is −1.25 and the artwork translates -15 diagram units.
Select 0.00: the text has two decimals without a sign, the artwork is centred, and Centre artwork is disabled.
Select +0.50 and +1.50: the actual positive values format as +0.50 and +1.50 and translate the artwork 6 and 18 diagram units.
Switch directly between negative and positive values, then use Centre artwork; inspect the final sign, decimal point and digits.
Inspect numeric announcements, live reduced motion and 320px/root 200% reflow without changing font size to hide overflow.
guidelines: Pass a numeric value and let format render its true sign and decimal precision.
Keep compact numeric values manageable at the selected type size and put units beside the component.
Update the diagram immediately from the accepted number; reel motion does not commit the correction.

signature-pad.summary: Draw a mark for Rosario edition 07, then undo, replay or export its actual strokes.
limits: Strokes are held in the current page; Clear removes the current drawing.
An empty pad disables replay and PNG/SVG export.
checks: Draw two real pointer strokes; undo, redo, clear and verify the changed drawing.
Download PNG and SVG and inspect the actual drawing; preserve focus and reduced-motion controls.
guidelines: Keep the drawing area and its actions accessible without moving the document horizontally.

image-compare.summary: Compare two original print proofs using the same controlled divider position.
limits: The divider moves from 0 to 100%; both complete SVG proofs remain available at the extremes.
checks: Drag the divider; use arrows, Home/End and reset to verify position and exposed proof.
guidelines: Describe the actual differences and preserve keyboard access to the divider.

logo-marquee.summary: Inspect three edition marks in a row, with tone selection and play and pause actions.
limits: Reduced motion makes the row static; the pause action is then unnecessary and hidden.
checks: Change between ink tones and single tone
Play and pause the row
guidelines: Keep repeated visual copies hidden from assistive technology; preserve the readable original list.

combobox.summary: Choose a Rosario edition's trim size and recalculate its sheet layout, sheet count and spare positions for 72 copies.
limits: The working area is 240 × 330 mm, with fixed orientation and no gutters. Poster exceeds that area and is disabled.
Typing narrows the available trims; the plan changes when a choice is committed. Clearing selection removes the plan.
checks: Initial Card selection shows four imposed copies and 18 sheets for 72 copies.
Choose Leaflet: one copy fits each sheet and the plan requires 72 sheets.
Search tall and choose Bookmark: five copies fit each sheet, with 15 sheets and three spare positions.
Find Poster and verify that its disabled option cannot replace the selection.
Search an unmatched term, recover by editing the query, then clear selection and choose a trim again.
Use keyboard search, arrows, Enter and Escape; verify focus and result state. Inspect enlarged text and live reduced motion.
guidelines: Update the drawing and the arithmetic from the same selected trim.
Give search keywords a concrete meaning, such as tall for Bookmark.
Explain why an unavailable option does not fit the model.

multi-select.summary: Select Mendoza ink layers to change the actual separation artwork and calculate impressions for a 60-sheet proof run.
limits: One visible chip and an overflow count summarize the selection; the listbox contains all four layer names.
Selection controls inclusion. The proof uses a fixed paint order, with one pass per selected layer.
checks: Initial Line and Tone selections produce two visible SVG separations and 120 impressions.
Select all four layers: the drawing includes Line, Tone, Grain and Type, and the total becomes 240 impressions.
Keep one layer selected and verify one separation and 60 impressions.
Clear selections: the sheet becomes blank and the total becomes zero impressions; select a layer to recover.
Open and toggle choices with the keyboard, then dismiss with Escape; inspect checked state, focus return and the overflow count.
Inspect the selected chip, count, menu and proof at enlarged text sizes and with live reduced motion.
guidelines: Show what each selected item adds to the shared composition.
Calculate totals from the same active layers that are rendered.
Keep the empty selection meaningful and provide a direct way to select again.

tag-input.summary: Add and remove keywords to filter a La Plata paper index, showing matching editions and their actual reference-sheet total.
limits: Every tag must match a record keyword after trimming and case folding. An empty tag list shows all six editions.
Enter, comma or blur commits one draft. Duplicate tags are compared without case sensitivity.
checks: Initial river filter shows River fold and Delta lines: two editions and 28 reference sheets.
Add fold: only River fold remains, with 12 reference sheets.
Try grain on its own: Clay grain and Night fold total 16 sheets.
Add an unknown tag, inspect the empty result and remove that tag to recover.
Remove every tag: all six editions appear and the total becomes 66 sheets.
Try a differently cased duplicate; use Backspace twice to select and remove the last tag, and verify input focus after removal.
Inspect wrapping tags, matching records and announcements at enlarged text sizes and with live reduced motion.
guidelines: State whether multiple tags use AND or OR matching.
Show record keywords so users can discover useful filters.
Make empty results recoverable by removing or editing the filters.

search-field.summary: Filters a fixed set of Argentine print-index entries by title, city, or process as the query changes.
limits: Matching ignores case and surrounding query whitespace across title, city and process. An empty query shows all six entries.
checks: Search by title, city, and process
Clear the field and confirm all entries return
Try a query with no matches
guidelines: Keep results tied to the query
Announce result changes without replacing the search field

inline-edit.summary: Edit a short title in place or a longer multiline note, with explicit save and cancel controls.
limits: The title wraps with the available width. Enter saves, Shift+Enter adds a line break and Escape cancels.
Blank titles are rejected by the validation callback; cancelling preserves the previous title.
checks: Edit, save and cancel each mode with keyboard and pointer.
Submit a blank proof title and verify its validation and recovery.
Inspect controls at narrow widths and enlarged text.
guidelines: Use the component's built-in save and cancel actions
Keep the edited value connected to visible content
demonstrates: Edit and validate the wrapping proof title.
Edit a multiline production note, then save or cancel without moving the action controls out of their editing rail.

chip-group.summary: Multiple selected process chips filter the visible print-index entries.
limits: Multiple selections use OR matching; clearing every chip shows all six entries.
checks: Select and clear each process chip
Confirm the visible entries and count update with the selection
guidelines: Use concise process labels
Keep filter results synchronized with the selected chips

breadcrumb.summary: Navigate a Rosario collection and its plate records through ancestor breadcrumbs and directory entries.
demonstrates: The initial path is Archive → River atlas → Plate 03, with the selected plate's artwork, process, paper and trim.
Ancestor crumbs and directory entries change the current heading, description and displayed directory or plate content.
The current crumb is noninteractive text with aria-current; navigation moves focus to the new content heading.
limits: Five local locations are available: Archive, River atlas and Plates 01–03.
checks: Initially verify two ancestor controls and one text-only current crumb, Plate 03, with Low-water grid and its relief-print details.
Choose River atlas: its heading and three plate entries replace the plate details, and River atlas becomes the noninteractive current crumb.
Choose Archive: its directory contains Open River atlas, with Archive as the only current crumb.
Open River atlas, then each plate; verify the complete path, current heading, artwork and process/paper/trim change together.
Check that the current crumb has no button or link action, including after rapid ancestor/child navigation.
Use Enter and Space on directory entries and ancestor controls; verify heading focus and enlarged-text/reduced-motion behaviour.
guidelines: Render the current location as text; give ancestor crumbs real route destinations or state-navigation callbacks.

pagination.summary: Browse 28 original Córdoba proof records, with four actual records per page and an exact visible-range total.
demonstrates: Seven edition studies supply plate identifiers, titles and printing processes for the visible list.
Previous, Next and numbered page controls select actual four-record slices while the five-number window follows the current page.
The range output updates with the list, and aria-current identifies the selected page.
limits: The fixed 28-record index has seven nonempty pages of four records each.
checks: On page 1, verify RL-01 Bank through RL-04 Silt, Showing proofs 1–4 of 28, Page 1 aria-current and disabled Previous page.
Choose Next page: TR-01 Corner through TR-04 Edge replace the records and the range becomes 5–8 of 28.
Choose Page 4: RS-01 Sleeper through RS-04 Track appear, the range becomes 13–16, and the numbered window shows pages 2–6.
Reach Page 7 through Next or the numbered window: CY-01 Arch through CY-04 Gate appear, the range becomes 25–28, and Next page is disabled.
Verify Page 7 aria-current and the 3–7 window, then use Previous and numbered pages to return through earlier slices.
Check that boundary buttons do not move outside pages 1–7 and each page presents exactly four records.
Traverse the controls with Tab, Enter and Space; inspect wrapped controls, focus, range announcements and live reduced motion at enlarged text sizes.
guidelines: Update the controlled page and the displayed collection slice from the same page state.

card.summary: Opens the Delta fold proof into the Card quick look, retaining the same original sheet artwork and paper/ink dimensions.
demonstrates: A titled card with print artwork, concise metadata, and an expandable quick look containing the proof's paper, ink-field, and fold details.
limits: Paper is 180 × 240 mm and the ink field is 120 × 180 mm in both card and quick look.
checks: Open the card and confirm the same artwork, dimensions, and edition details appear
Close the quick look and confirm it returns to the card
guidelines: Keep the card itself as the quick-look trigger
Use the detail panel for information about the same specimen

scroll-area.summary: Lists twelve named paper stocks with city, process, gsm, and sheet count in a bounded vertical viewport.
demonstrates: Native scrolling in a labelled viewport; the edge callback changes a short status hint as more rows become available or the list ends.
limits: All twelve entries remain in the list; there is no pagination or remote loading.
The endpoint hint reflects whether content remains below the viewport.
checks: Scroll through all twelve records and reach Orchard 15
Confirm the hint changes to End of stock list at the bottom and back when scrolling upward
guidelines: Keep each record readable when its text wraps
Retain the final row in the scrollable content

resizable-panels.summary: Resize a two-pane proof layout and choose which original plate appears in the proof pane.
demonstrates: The requested starting ratio is 35/65; the divider and output report the actual settled shares when pane minima constrain the layout.
Choose P01, P02, or P03 to update the proof title and inline SVG artwork.
Resize the panes with the divider and read their settled shares.
limits: The first pane is collapsible; the proof pane remains available.
On narrow panes, the proof canvas scrolls locally so its type keeps the selected size.
checks: Choose each plate and confirm its title and proof artwork change together.
Resize with pointer and keyboard; verify each pane respects its minimum and the first pane can collapse and restore.
Check the settled share output after resizing and at a narrow viewport.
At 320px and text 200%, verify complete P01/P02/P03 codes, keyboard pan of the proof canvas, and actual shares matching the divider and output.
guidelines: Give the group a definite height and keep its panel IDs stable while the group is mounted.
Collapse the plate list when the proof needs more room on a narrow screen.

carousel.summary: Browse Riverbend, Railrhythm, and Openframe as three original inline SVG studies.
demonstrates: The carousel controls update the selected study title and detail.
Each slide contains distinct original vector artwork.
limits: The carousel does not autoplay.
checks: Use the carousel arrows and slide controls; confirm the selected title and detail match the artwork.
Check keyboard navigation and drag selection at a narrow viewport.
guidelines: Keep the controlled slide index and its associated description synchronized; use this pattern for a short ordered set of peers.

dialog.summary: Edit a Rosario print title in a modal dialog, committing the proof heading with Save or discarding the draft with Cancel.
demonstrates: The committed title and editable draft are separate values.
Save title updates the actual heading and closes the dialog; dismissing the editor restores the committed value for the next open.
limits: The title contains at most 48 characters and must remain nonempty after trimming.
Cancel, Close, Escape and outside dismissal discard the draft.
checks: Open Edit print title, enter a new title and save; verify the proof heading changes and focus returns to the trigger.
Change the draft and cancel; verify the heading stays committed and reopening restores that value.
Repeat draft dismissal through Close, Escape and an outside click.
Submit an empty or whitespace-only draft; verify the associated error, retained dialog and unchanged heading, then recover with a valid title.
Verify Close receives initial focus, Tab and Shift+Tab contain focus, Enter submits a valid title, and the enlarged dialog preserves its layout during a stable-open reduced-motion preference change.
guidelines: Keep drafts separate from committed content until Save succeeds.
Validate before closing and make every dismissal path follow the same rollback rule.

drawer.summary: Choose one of three paper stocks in a drawer and update the Córdoba proof's stock, weight and finish.
demonstrates: The owned Select reads and updates the same stock record used by the visible proof metadata.
Smooth is 120 gsm, Cotton is 160 gsm and Rag is 220 gsm.
limits: Selection applies immediately and remains selected when the drawer closes.
checks: Open Choose paper and verify initial Cotton, 160 gsm and Soft, uncoated metadata.
Choose Smooth and Rag; verify the matching 120/220 gsm weights and Calendered/Textured finishes.
Close with Done, Close drawer, Escape and outside dismissal; verify the selected record remains and focus returns to Choose paper.
Check keyboard Select operation inside the modal, focus containment/return and the actual header drag behaviour.
Inspect drawer content, nested Select and close controls at narrow/enlarged sizes and with live reduced motion.
guidelines: Keep the selected name, weight and finish tied to one record.
State clearly that selection applies immediately so dismissal does not imply rollback.

popover.summary: Choose one or two ink passes in a popover, changing the actual Mendoza separation layers and impression total.
demonstrates: One pass renders one SVG layer and 60 impressions; two passes render two layers and 120 impressions.
The result remains visible outside the popover.
limits: The proof run is fixed at 60 sheets; each selected pass corresponds to one separation layer.
The choice applies immediately and remains after dismissal.
checks: Open Ink passes and choose 2; verify two actual SVG pass groups and 120 impressions.
Choose 1 again; verify the second layer is removed and the total returns to 60 impressions.
Dismiss with Done, Escape and an outside click; reopen and verify the current choice.
Check keyboard entry, the nested Select, trigger focus return and panel collision handling.
Inspect the anchored panel and controls at narrow/enlarged sizes and with reduced motion.
guidelines: Derive the artwork and arithmetic from the same pass value.
Keep the result available after the settings panel closes and keep the trigger's anchor stable.

hover-card.summary: Inspect the read-only process and material specifications of La Plata plate LP-07, Brick arch.
demonstrates: The trigger reference and preview title come from the same plate record.
The preview exposes Drypoint, Copper plate, Rag 180 gsm and 105 × 148 mm trim.
limits: The preview contains one static, read-only plate record.
Overflowing specifications scroll locally; navigation keys on the focused trigger scroll the open preview without moving focus.
checks: Hover or keyboard-focus Plate LP-07; verify LP-07, Brick arch and all four matching specifications.
Move the pointer into the card and back; verify the preview remains usable through the existing intent/grace behaviour.
Dismiss with Escape or leave the trigger/card; verify focus stays on the trigger during informational preview use.
Inspect narrow/enlarged content and live reduced motion; confirm that the card has no action or form controls.
When the specifications overflow the available height, keep focus on Plate LP-07 and use Home/End or Page Up/Page Down to reach both ends of the actual preview.
guidelines: Use one record for the trigger identity and the expanded details.
Keep informational previews read-only; the trigger retains focus.

tooltip.summary: Explain a named Crop marks button that adds or removes cut guides on an original Tucumán print diagram.
demonstrates: The owned button keeps its visible accessible name and pressed state while Tooltip supplies supplementary help.
Toggling changes four actual crop-mark corner paths around a 140 × 200 mm trim.
limits: The trim stays at 140 × 200 mm; the button controls only its crop marks.
checks: Hover or focus Crop marks and verify the Cut guides. tooltip.
Activate with a click, Enter and Space; verify aria-pressed, the SVG corner marks and the visible on/off result.
Dismiss the tooltip with Escape and leave/blur the trigger; verify the button retains its name and operation.
Inspect tooltip placement, focus and mark visibility at narrow/enlarged sizes and with reduced motion.
guidelines: Keep the control named independently of its tooltip.
Use pressed state and the actual drawing to communicate the toggle; the tooltip only explains its purpose.

dropdown-menu.summary: Menu commands show or hide crop guides, reverse ink and paper, or restore the original proof state.
demonstrates: Selecting a menu item changes the print SVG and its visible state description.
limits: Changes affect only this proof preview.
Reset restores visible crop guides and dark ink on light paper.
checks: Open the menu and toggle crop guides
Reverse ink and paper, then reset the proof
guidelines: Name each item for the action it performs
Keep the SVG state and status description synchronized

context-menu.summary: A context menu on the original plate changes its orientation and margin width, and the SVG updates to match.
demonstrates: The plate is the menu target; its portrait/landscape proportions and ink-frame margins follow the chosen actions.
limits: Actions update the visible plate layout in this preview only.
The component also supports its built-in click and keyboard triggers.
checks: Open the menu on the plate with a right-click
Choose each orientation and margin option and inspect the updated plate
Focus the plate and open its menu with Shift+F10
guidelines: Keep the menu attached to the object it changes
Avoid actions that imply deletion, download, or persistence

command-palette.summary: Searches five authored Argentine print records by title, city, process, or paper, then updates the selected record display.
demonstrates: Choosing a result replaces the selected heading, SVG mark, city, process, and paper specification.
limits: Search covers five fixed records in this preview.
The command results are local selections and do not fetch or persist records.
checks: Search by city or process and choose a result
Search for an absent term, then clear the query and confirm results return
Verify the chosen record updates the heading, artwork, and specifications
guidelines: Keep result descriptions tied to the displayed record
Use the command palette's built-in empty and recovery states

metric-card.summary: Compares accepted sheets across two consecutive seven-run periods for a Rosario print edition.
demonstrates: The current seven run values total 1,006 sheets; the previous seven total 820.
The displayed change is +22.7%, calculated from those two totals.
limits: The comparison covers the two displayed seven-run lists.
checks: Sum each seven-run list and confirm totals of 1,006 and 820.
Confirm the percent change uses the previous period as its denominator and rounds to +22.7%.
guidelines: Compare equal-length periods and name the unit and window in the label or context.
Keep the source values available so a displayed total and change can be checked.

sparkline.summary: Scrub seven labelled Córdoba proof runs to inspect the spoiled-sheet count.
demonstrates: The sequence is 8, 7, 9, 6, 6, 4, and 3 spoiled sheets across Runs 08–14.
The latest value is 3 sheets; the first-to-last change is −62.5%.
Pointer and keyboard scrubbing expose the selected run label and value.
The plot uses the default accent tone; a labelled change states the decrease without assigning a status colour to the series.
limits: Runs have equal spacing; the plot represents their sequence rather than elapsed calendar time.
checks: Scrub every point and verify the run label and spoiled-sheet value.
Confirm the displayed change is calculated from 8 to 3 sheets.
guidelines: Label each point when users need to relate a value to a specific run or date.
Keep the current value, unit, and direction of change available in text as well as the line.

gauge.summary: Shows a Mendoza proof measurement against three explicit registration thresholds.
demonstrates: The sample measurement is 0.18 mm on a 0–0.50 mm scale.
Below 0.25 mm the state is within tolerance; 0.25–0.39 mm calls for adjustment; 0.40 mm or more means stop and realign.
Threshold meanings are written beside the gauge and are not conveyed by color alone.
The physical value 0.18 mm occupies 36% of the 0–0.50 mm range; the gauge displays that normalized percentage.
limits: The thresholds apply to the displayed 0–0.50 mm reference range.
checks: Confirm 0.18 mm maps to 36% of the 0–0.50 mm range and the Within tolerance threshold.
Check that each threshold boundary and action is readable without relying on color.
guidelines: Choose thresholds from the domain rule and state the unit and boundary values.
Pair each tone with a named state and keep the threshold meaning available in text.

tree-view.summary: Browse original Rosario, Córdoba and Mendoza plates in a tree that changes a contact sheet and its reference-sheet inventory.
demonstrates: Three place folders contain two plates each; the initial overview displays all six original line studies and 240 reference sheets.
Selecting a folder shows its two drawings and inventory; selecting a plate shows its drawing, process, paper and sheet count.
Arrow navigation moves focus independently of selection; activating a folder selects it and toggles its children.
limits: Six fixed plate records are arranged in three place folders. Expansion changes the tree; it does not clear the selected contact sheet.
checks: Initially Rosario is expanded, no treeitem is selected, and Cabinet overview shows six plates and 240 reference sheets.
Activate Rosario: its two plates remain in the contact sheet with 72 sheets, while the folder collapses.
Expand Rosario with Arrow Right, focus Landing without activating it, and verify that the contact sheet still shows the selected folder.
Activate Landing: only its line study and RQ-01 Relief/Cotton inventory remain, totaling 48 sheets.
Select Córdoba and Mendoza in turn: their two-plate inventories total 96 and 72 sheets respectively.
Exercise Arrow Up/Down, Left/Right, Home/End, Enter and Space; verify focus, expansion and aria-selected match their separate operations.
Inspect labels, selected drawings, complete inventory text and focus at 320px with enlarged text and live reduced motion.
guidelines: Give every tree node a stable identifier independent of its displayed label.
Keep focus movement separate from selection and retain selected content when its branch collapses.
Repeat complete plate details in the content area so the inventory remains readable.

filter-toolbar.summary: Combine Place, Process and Paper filters to find actual plates and recalculate their reference-sheet quantities.
demonstrates: The initial Rosario filter returns Landing and Tide stair, totaling 72 reference sheets.
Filters use AND matching; a new value replaces the prior value for that field.
Removing chips and clearing all filters update the visible inventory and can recover an empty result.
limits: The local index has six records, three places, three processes and two paper stocks. Each field has at most one active value.
checks: Initially verify two of six plates and 72 reference sheets, with the Place: Rosario chip.
Replace Place with Mendoza: Canal turn and Vine grid remain, totaling 72 sheets and one Place chip.
Add Process: Relief: only Vine grid remains, with 42 sheets.
Add Paper: Rag: verify zero plates, zero sheets and the recovery instruction.
Remove Paper: recover Vine grid; clear all filters to show all six plates and 240 sheets.
Choose a field and value by keyboard, navigate back to fields, dismiss with Escape and remove a chip; verify focus and active value indications.
Inspect the menu, wrapping chips, inventory and empty result at narrow widths, enlarged text and live reduced motion.
guidelines: State that active filters combine with AND.
Replace a field value rather than accumulating contradictory values for the same field.
Calculate totals from the same records that appear in the results and keep empty results recoverable.

sortable-data-table.summary: Sort plate quantities and select records to assemble a live packing slip with actual paper stocks and sheet totals.
demonstrates: The numeric Sheets column initially orders quantities 24, 30, 36, 42, 48 and 60.
Column sorting changes table order while stable identifiers retain selected plates.
Selected rows populate a packing slip with complete plate details and a derived total; no selection produces an empty slip.
limits: All six records remain in the table. Selection changes the local slip; sorting does not determine its inventory order.
checks: Initially verify Tide stair first, Arch seam last, Sheets aria-sort ascending and an empty packing slip with zero sheets.
Activate Sheets sorting again: verify descending order from 60 to 24 and aria-sort descending.
Select Landing and Tide stair: the slip shows their two records, Cotton and Rag stocks, and 72 sheets.
Sort by Plate or Place: the same two records stay selected and the slip total stays 72.
Select all rows: verify six selected records, a checked select-all control and 240 sheets; clear selection to recover the empty slip.
Check the mixed select-all state with a subset, Shift selection across sorted rows, row checkbox Space, supported arrow navigation and Escape clearing.
Inspect table/card layout, accessible column and checkbox names, slip text, focus and live reduced motion at narrow widths and enlarged text.
guidelines: Sort numeric quantities as numbers while retaining stable row keys.
Keep selection independent of the current sort order.
Show quantities and paper stock for every selected record rather than reporting only a selected count.

reorderable-list.summary: Reorder four original city studies to recalculate the page ranges and block diagram of a 24-page walking booklet.
demonstrates: Four sections contain 4, 8, 4 and 8 pages, and retain their own lengths while their order changes.
Dragging a handle or using Arrow Up/Down changes the actual reading sequence, numbered index and proportional page blocks.
Reset order resets the section order and page ranges.
limits: The booklet has four fixed-length sections and 24 pages. This model assigns consecutive reading pages; it does not calculate press imposition or binding signatures.
checks: Initially verify Quay fold 1–4, Stone steps 5–12, Canal ledger 13–16 and Vine screen 17–24, with Reset order disabled.
Focus the Stone steps handle and press Arrow Up: verify Stone steps 1–8, Quay fold 9–12, Canal ledger 13–16 and Vine screen 17–24.
Verify the moved handle retains focus, its position label updates and the opening-section output becomes Stone steps.
Move the first section upward and the last section downward: neither operation crosses the list boundary.
Drag Vine screen to the beginning: verify it occupies pages 1–8 and the page blocks and index follow the same new order.
Restore the original sequence: verify all four initial ranges return and the reset control becomes disabled.
Inspect handle accessibility, drag/keyboard distinctions, complete page index, narrow enlarged text and live reduced motion while moving a section.
guidelines: Preserve section identity and page length when reordering.
Derive the page index and diagram from the same ordered list.
Offer the existing keyboard handle operation alongside pointer dragging and a direct reset.

bar-chart.summary: Shows sheets discarded across seven Rosario proof runs, with the chart's average line as a reference.
demonstrates: The sample run counts are 12, 9, 15, 8, 6, 10, and 5 sheets.
The seven runs total 65 sheets; their arithmetic mean is 65/7, about 9.3 sheets per run.
limits: These are sample press-worksheet values, not a published production record.
The average is a reference across the seven displayed runs and does not describe a target or acceptable limit.
checks: Confirm the seven values sum to 65 sheets and the average is 65/7.
Scrub each bar and verify its proof-run label and sheet count.
guidelines: Use a bar chart for period-by-period comparisons of one measure.
Name the period and unit, and distinguish an observed average from a target.

activity-heatmap.summary: Browse a Mendoza proof log from January 5 through March 1, 2026; select a day to read its recorded checks.
demonstrates: The eight-week log contains 56 dates and 126 registration checks in total.
February 16, 2026 starts week seven in this Monday-first view and has 2 recorded checks.
Threshold upper bounds are 1, 2, and 4 checks; counts above 4 use the highest level.
limits: The worksheet is sample data, not a live press log.
Zero-count days mean no checks were recorded for that sample date; they do not establish that a press was idle.
checks: Confirm the date range is 56 days, January 5 through March 1 inclusive, and the counts sum to 126.
Select February 16, 2026 and verify the adjacent readout says 2 registration checks.
Check the written unit and threshold ranges alongside the heatmap; intensity alone does not define their meaning.
guidelines: Use a heatmap to reveal activity rhythm across dates, not to compare exact values more precisely than its legend allows.
State the time range, unit, threshold boundaries, and meaning of zero-count dates.

line-chart.summary: Compares misregistered-sheet counts for two plates across seven Córdoba proof pulls.
demonstrates: Each point counts sheets outside the registration marks in a 20-sheet proof pull.
Plate A changes from 8 sheets in proof 01 to 3 in proof 07; Plate B changes from 11 to 4.
The plotted values are separate plate counts; they are not a combined total or a percentage.
limits: The proof pulls are sample worksheet data, not a production quality report.
The series show association over proof order only; they do not explain why counts changed.
checks: Inspect all seven proof labels and verify the two plotted sequences against the source rows.
Toggle each legend series and confirm the remaining line retains its own values and label.
guidelines: Use a line chart when the sequence and direction across ordered observations matter.
Define each series and denominator clearly; do not imply a cause from a trend alone.

donut-chart.summary: Shows how a sample Buenos Aires print plan allocates 1,200 sheets among four paper uses.
demonstrates: Cover stock is 640 sheets, text stock 360, proof reserve 120, and make-ready 80.
The four parts sum to 1,200 sheets and represent one whole allocation.
limits: These are sample planning values, not a procurement record or production commitment.
The chart compares shares of this allocation; it does not show paper weight or stock specifications.
checks: Confirm the legend values sum to 1,200 sheets and the chart center reports the same total.
Inspect each legend entry and verify its category and quantity remain available without relying on segment color.
guidelines: Use a donut chart only when categories are parts of the same whole.
Name the whole and unit, and keep exact category values available beside the segments.

streamgraph.previewTitle: Ink use by plate · eight press weeks
streamgraph.summary: Compares the changing mix of four separation inks in a Rosario sample worksheet across eight weeks.
demonstrates: Weekly values are in litres for black, cyan, magenta, and yellow plates; the four values form each week's total.
The eight-week totals are 333 L black, 105 L cyan, 94 L magenta, and 86 L yellow, for 618 L overall.
The streamgraph shows relative mix and total volume; its layers can be toggled with the native legend.
limits: These are sample press-worksheet quantities, not metered or published production records.
The curve between weekly observations does not represent additional measurements.
checks: Confirm there are eight ordered weeks from April 6 through May 25, 2026.
Sum the weekly plate values and verify the four totals sum to 618 L.
Toggle each legend entry and verify the other layers remain visible and identified.
guidelines: Use a streamgraph to compare how parts of a total change together when exact point comparison is secondary.
Name each layer and unit, and state whether the total changes over time.

brush-chart.summary: Browse 56 daily sample weights in a Córdoba recovery log, with two dated ledger annotations.
demonstrates: The series has one daily value in kilograms from June 1 through July 26, 2026; the values range from 0 to 44 kg.
The June 1–July 26 period contains 56 consecutive observations.
The overview brush selects a date window; the chart's reset control restores the full range. Its default minimum window is seven days.
limits: These are sample recovery-log values, not a live scale reading or verified recycling record.
The Edition 12 and Collection markers are sample ledger annotations, not claims of a real event.
checks: Confirm dates are ascending, consecutive, and cover June 1–July 26, 2026.
Inspect the Edition 12 marker on July 2 and the Collection marker on July 15.
Move and resize the brush, verify its window stays within the data range, and reset to the full 56 days.
guidelines: Use a brush chart for a dense time series where the overview and a selectable close range are both useful.
Label the unit, date window, and meaning of annotations; keep daily values ordered.

ridgeline.summary: Compares the distribution of signed trim-mark offsets for three sample stock lots measured in Mendoza.
demonstrates: Each stock lot has 16 observations in millimetres, with a shared displayed domain from −0.50 to +0.50 mm.
Negative measurements are before the trim mark and positive measurements are beyond it; zero is the mark.
The ridges summarize distributions rather than plotting every sample as a separate point.
limits: The measurements are sample worksheet observations, not a calibration certificate or tolerance claim.
The displayed domain bounds the comparison; it does not define an acceptable production range.
checks: Confirm three stock lots are listed and each has 16 source measurements.
Check the horizontal domain and signed millimetre labels include values on both sides of zero.
Focus or hover each ridge and confirm its summary names the matching stock lot.
guidelines: Use ridgelines to compare the shapes and spread of multiple distributions measured on the same scale.
State the sample size, unit, reference point, and any domain bounds.

treemap.previewTitle: Recovered paper by stock and use
treemap.summary: Breaks a sample Buenos Aires edition reconciliation into paper stocks and specific uses; tile area is recovered mass.
demonstrates: The six use-level quantities are 42, 28, 36, 18, 24, and 12 kg, totaling 160 kg.
Branch totals are 70 kg coated paper, 54 kg uncoated paper, and 36 kg cover board.
The second measure is the recorded recovery share: 70–94% across use-level entries.
limits: The reconciliation is sample data, not a measured environmental impact or verified recycling claim.
Tile area encodes kilograms; shading encodes the separate recovery-share measure and is not a second size.
checks: Confirm the six use values sum to 160 kg and each stock branch equals its child total.
Inspect the recovery-share scale from 70% to 94% and distinguish it from tile area.
Zoom into a stock branch, then use the breadcrumb to return to the edition total.
guidelines: Use a treemap for hierarchical parts when relative size is the primary comparison.
Label any color measure separately from the area measure and ensure branch totals equal their children.

waffle-chart.summary: Shows how a sample La Plata edition allocates a 1,000-copy print run across five destinations.
demonstrates: The allocation is 420 bookshop, 260 subscriber, 180 library, 90 print-fair, and 50 archive copies.
The values sum to 1,000 copies; a 10 × 10 grid assigns one cell to each 1% of the total, or 10 copies.
The native legend and cell focus expose a category's count and share.
limits: These are sample allocation values, not sales, shipments, or confirmed reservations.
Each cell represents a share of the whole, not an individually tracked copy.
checks: Confirm the five values total 1,000 and their shares are 42%, 26%, 18%, 9%, and 5%.
Inspect all legend entries and focus categories to read their counts and shares.
guidelines: Use a waffle chart when a whole can be divided into countable equal shares.
Choose the grid resolution to match the precision of the source and state the whole and unit.

slope-chart.summary: Compares sample minutes for five print-finishing stations between editions 11 and 12.
demonstrates: Station values in minutes are: prepress 18→15, plate setup 32→27, press registration 46→38, binding setup 25→29, and packing setup 14→12.
Four station times decrease; binding setup increases by 4 minutes. The sum across these five stations changes from 135 to 121 minutes.
The native chart displays both period values and rank changes.
limits: These are sample worksheet timings, not a measured productivity study.
The comparison covers only two editions and does not establish why any station time changed.
checks: Verify each station's Edition 11 and Edition 12 value and its signed change.
Confirm binding setup rises by 4 minutes and the five-station sums are 135 and 121 minutes.
Focus each station and confirm the highlighted values and rank labels identify the same row.
guidelines: Use a slope chart to compare the same items at exactly two ordered moments.
Name both periods, units, and item identities; report rank movement separately from value change.

calendar.summary: Select a weekday sign-off date in a Rosario sample proof schedule for November 2026.
demonstrates: The calendar opens in November 2026 with November 12 selected.
The selectable window is November 2–December 4 inclusive; Saturdays and Sundays are disabled.
The sample month view is controlled, so its previous and next month controls update the displayed month.
limits: The dates are a sample production schedule, not a real booking calendar.
No event availability or external calendar service is queried.
checks: Verify November 12, 2026 is initially selected and the adjacent status names that date.
Confirm dates before November 2, after December 4, and weekend dates cannot be selected.
Navigate from November to December and back; confirm navigation changes the month without changing the selected date.
guidelines: Use Calendar when users need a persistent month grid and direct date selection.
Explain disabled dates and constrain selection to the actual scheduling window.

date-picker.summary: Choose a weekday delivery date in a bounded Córdoba receiving window, with one reserved calibration day.
demonstrates: The selected date starts at November 10, 2026; the allowed window is November 9–20 inclusive.
Weekend dates and November 12 are disabled; the description identifies the press-calibration reservation.
The picker is controlled and the nearby live status follows a selected date or a cleared value.
limits: The receiving window and calibration reservation are sample schedule data.
The picker does not create a delivery order or contact a supplier.
checks: Verify November 10, 2026 is initially displayed and the local status agrees.
Confirm dates outside November 9–20, weekends, and November 12 cannot be chosen.
Choose an available weekday and verify the field and adjacent status update to the same date; clear and check the empty status.
When the picker shows “Scroll for more dates,” scroll horizontally or move through dates with the arrow keys.
guidelines: Use min/max bounds for the real booking window and disabledDates for unavailable dates within it.
Keep the reason for a special blocked date available in the field description.

time-picker.summary: Select and display a local workshop handoff time in 24-hour format at 30-minute intervals.
demonstrates: The initial time is 14:30; the component offers all 48 half-hour points in a day.
The selected value is controlled and updates the adjacent status after a choice.
The time and supporting copy specify local workshop time; no timezone conversion is applied.
limits: The time is a sample local schedule value, not an appointment or calendar event.
The picker accepts the full day and does not enforce a shift-length or business-hours rule.
checks: Verify 14:30 is the initial value and the status matches it.
Choose an earlier and later option using the list and arrow keys; confirm the field and status match each selected HH:mm value.
Confirm the interval is 30 minutes and the format is 24-hour.
guidelines: Choose minuteStep to match the scheduling precision the workflow can honor.
State whether a displayed time is local and apply timezone handling at the integration boundary when needed.

date-range-picker.summary: Apply one of two sample La Plata production windows in a single-month date-range picker.
demonstrates: The initial applied range is November 9–13, 2026, inclusive.
The Proof week preset selects November 9–13; Press week selects November 16–20.
Selection is controlled by the applied onChange result; the nearby status reports the committed range.
limits: Both ranges are fixed sample presets, not live production availability.
The picker has November 2–27 bounds and displays one month; no external schedule is read or changed.
checks: Verify the initial trigger and status show November 9–13, 2026.
Choose Press week and apply; confirm the applied status changes to November 16–20.
Choose Proof week and apply; confirm the status returns to November 9–13. Canceling an edit must leave the applied status unchanged.
Confirm dates outside the configured bounds cannot be applied.
guidelines: Use a range picker for workflows that need a start and end date selected together.
Name preset ranges, constrain them to the valid window, and distinguish a draft selection from an applied range.

toast-stack.summary: Records a local sample proof check, offers Undo in the stacked notice, and keeps the result under the visitor's control.
demonstrates: Record sample proof check increments the local counter and adds an informational toast with an Undo action.
Undo decrements the local counter and updates that same toast to a notice without an action.
The four newest notices are retained; adding a fifth evicts the oldest. Each original notice has infinite duration until Undo or dismissal; its updated notice uses 4,500 ms.
limits: The counter and notices live only in component state; no workshop record is transmitted or saved.
The updated notice closes on the component's real duration unless dismissed sooner.
checks: Record one check and confirm the local counter and open-notice count each increase by one.
Choose Undo and confirm the counter decreases by one and the same toast changes to 'Sample check removed'.
Record two notices, dismiss all, and verify the stack count returns to zero without changing the check counter.
guidelines: Use a toast stack for brief results of local or completed actions, and describe the action outcome plainly.
Offer Undo only when it reverses a real local change; keep the underlying state and toast copy in sync.

toast.summary: Open a standalone, dismissible local reminder about checking crop marks on a sample proof sheet.
demonstrates: The button opens the controlled toast; dismissing it or letting its built-in 4,500 ms duration elapse closes it.
The reminder contains no saved proof state and makes no claim that a check has already been completed.
limits: The reminder is local to the preview and does not check a proof file.
The standalone Toast accepts title, description and duration; it does not expose a result type or action slot.
checks: Activate Show local proof reminder and verify the reminder title and instruction appear.
Dismiss the toast and confirm the trigger can open it again; leave it open to confirm the component's timed close behavior.
guidelines: Use a standalone toast for a short, non-blocking message that does not require a choice.
Avoid success language when the message is only a reminder and no work has been completed.

notification-center.summary: Filter, read, and dismiss three local sample print-workshop updates without person records or remote delivery.
demonstrates: The list starts with two unread and one read sample update, each with a title, description, time, and tone.
The native All and Unread views, individual read state, bulk Mark all read, and dismissal update the component's local list.
The adjacent status reports individual read and dismissal callbacks.
limits: Times and events are static sample entries, not live workshop activity.
Read and dismiss changes remain inside the component instance; they are not persisted or sent to a service.
checks: Open the notification center and confirm its unread count begins at two.
Switch to Unread and confirm only the two unread entries remain; mark one read and confirm the view/count updates.
Use Mark all read and verify the unread view is empty and the status reflects the latest callback.
Dismiss an item in All and verify it disappears from the panel and the local status names it.
guidelines: Use a notification center for updates that remain available for later review, with explicit read and dismissal states.
Keep times, statuses, and any actor information tied to real sources when integrating beyond sample data.

announcement-bar.summary: Manually browse two sample production-window notices, reveal their local notes, and dismiss or restore the bar.
demonstrates: Previous and next controls move between the November 9–13 proof-review message and November 16–20 press-window message.
Automatic rotation is disabled; the action button opens local notes with both windows.
Dismissal hides the controlled bar and Show schedule notices restores it. No persistence id is set.
limits: Both windows and notes are sample schedule copy, not confirmed production bookings.
The preview does not navigate to a schedule service and dismissal is not remembered between visits.
checks: Confirm the bar starts on the proof-review message and next/previous controls select the other message and return.
Activate Show proof notes or Show press notes and verify the local schedule notes appear; close them with Hide schedule notes.
Dismiss the bar and use Show schedule notices to restore it.
guidelines: Use an announcement bar for a short, relevant notice with a direct action when one exists.
Keep rotation controllable and make dismissal persistence an explicit product choice.

cookie-consent.summary: Compare accept, reject, and save choices for one required and two optional sample categories; reopen or reset the local choice.
demonstrates: Essential settings are required; proof-display preferences and aggregate guide counts are optional and begin off.
Accept all, Essential only, or a saved custom selection produces a controlled choice and an adjacent status.
The component's reopen button returns to preferences; Reset sample choice clears the controlled value and restores the initial bar.
limits: No storageKey is supplied, so choices are not written to localStorage; the preview has no cookie or tracking scripts connected.
Optional category descriptions describe hypothetical site behavior, not active collection.
checks: Confirm the initial bar offers review, allow-optional, and essential-only choices.
Accept optional categories and verify the selected count is two; reopen preferences and save with both optional switches off, then verify the count is zero.
Choose Essential only and verify required remains enabled while optional categories are off.
Use Reset sample choice and verify the panel returns to its undecided state.
guidelines: Keep required categories on, make refusal as accessible as acceptance, and explain each optional category plainly.
Connect consent state to actual storage or scripts only when those integrations exist; do not imply persistence without it.

empty-states.summary: Four original print-workflow examples recover from empty filters, notes, a proof tray and a closed folio through real local state changes.
demonstrates: Index starts with Stencil and Rag filters matching no plate; clearing them reveals three stored records with 26 reference sheets. Restoring filters returns to zero.
Notes adds or removes a La Plata LP-02 registration note with a 0.2 mm offset toward the gripper.
Tray adds or removes the six-sheet Rosario Quay sequence packet and lists its reference, location and actual sheet count.
Folio opens or closes two stored Mendoza plate records totaling 16 sheets.

The four composite tabs support Left/Right, Home and End; each tab retains its local changes. RAMS icons identify each empty state; a brief transition preserves feedback without decorative illustrations.
limits: All records, filters and notes are local sample data; no remote request or storage occurs.
The complete block takes no props. Its actions change local models immediately; they do not simulate reconnection, delivery, mail or an external search.
checks: Clear and restore Index filters; compare visible record IDs and the 26-sheet total.
Add the LP-02 note, switch tabs and return, then remove it; check the 0.2 mm value and focus.
Add and remove the Quay sequence packet; verify its record and six-sheet total.
Open and close Canal folio; verify both record IDs and their 6 + 10 = 16 sheet total.
Use arrow keys, Home and End to move between tabs; verify selected tab, panel name and preserved state.
guidelines: Explain the actual empty state and provide an action that changes the relevant local model.
Show the records behind a recovery result, and preserve independent state when moving between views.

mention-input.summary: Compose a local proof note with role-only sample @ handles and print-workshop # channels, then inspect its structured mention serialization.
demonstrates: The input offers two role-only sample handles and three channels; no person portraits are supplied.
Selecting an @ handle or # channel creates a structured MentionValue entry with its text range.
Post note and Enter submit the current text, clear the editor, and show the submitted note plus its default serialized IDs.
Clear note removes only the local preview entry.
limits: Handles and channels are sample labels, not real accounts or destinations.
Posting does not notify a person, publish a message, or write data to a service.
checks: Type @ and choose a role handle; verify the inserted mention is present in the structured value.
Type # and choose a channel; verify the local note displays the selected channel and serialized <#id> token.
Submit non-empty text using Enter and the button; verify both paths show the note and clear the input.
Submit blank text and verify no posted note is created; clear a posted note and verify it disappears.
guidelines: Use structured mention values when text references selectable people or channels and preserve offsets as text changes.
Keep mention suggestions limited to the accounts and destinations the consuming product can actually resolve.

rich-text-editor.summary: Edit an original proof-note draft and inspect the editor's live text, Markdown, and undo/redo availability.
demonstrates: The initial note uses supported defaultMarkdown with a heading, paragraph, and bulleted checks.
The component retains its built-in selection formatting and link toolbar, slash block menu, Markdown shortcuts, and keyboard undo/redo.
onChange supplies HTML, Markdown, plain text, and empty state; the scene displays current text length and Markdown after edits.
onHistoryChange reports whether undo and redo are available.
limits: The note exists only in the editor instance; no save, export, or server integration is present.
The displayed character count is plain text length, not a word count or publishing limit.
checks: Confirm the initial Edition 18 heading, trim instruction, and two checklist items appear.
Edit text and use a formatting control; verify the local character count and Markdown output follow the edit.
Use the slash menu to add a supported block, then undo and redo; verify history availability updates.
Create a link using the selection toolbar and inspect the resulting Markdown without navigating away.
guidelines: Keep the editor editable and preserve its native formatting, block, link, and history controls.
Treat editor output as local draft content until a real persistence action is provided.

billing-toggle.summary: Switch between monthly and annual sample prices for a print-workshop reference plan and update the local quote.
demonstrates: Monthly sample price is ARS 36,000 per month; annual sample price is ARS 360,000 per year.
Twelve monthly payments total ARS 432,000; the annual sample saves ARS 72,000, or 16.7%, and averages ARS 30,000 per month.
The quote follows the selected period and shows the exact annual savings and percentage with the annual price.
limits: All prices are fictional sample values, not a real offer or current price list.
The toggle changes local display state only; it does not charge, subscribe, or save a billing choice.
checks: Confirm Annual is selected initially and the displayed amount is ARS 360,000 per year with ARS 30,000 monthly equivalent.
Select Monthly and verify ARS 36,000 per month appears and the annual savings line is absent.
Select Annual and verify the result shows ARS 72,000 yearly savings and 16.7%.
guidelines: Keep billing-period labels, price cadence, and savings denominator explicit.
Treat a period toggle as a display choice unless a separate, confirmed subscription action exists.

Import `BillingPrice` from `./rams/components/motion-billing-toggle` to animate a displayed price. Pass `amount` and optional `was` in major currency units, so 360000 means ARS 360,000. For example, `<BillingPrice amount={360000} currency="ARS " period="per year" was={432000} />`. The optional `decimals` prop controls fractional display and `className` supports styling.

radio-cards.summary: Choose a sample cover-paper stock from radio cards and read the selected stock in a local docket status.
