demonstrates: The initial selection is Matte coated, 170 gsm; Uncoated offset, 120 gsm is another selectable option.
Recycled blend test is disabled with a reason specific to the sample docket.
The list-layout ARIA radio group updates its selected value and the adjacent status; a hidden form field uses edition18-cover-stock as its name.
limits: Stock names, weights, and availability are sample editorial choices, not a supplier specification or live inventory.
Selecting a card changes local state only and does not place a materials order.
Required is announced by the ARIA group; the hidden field is not a native required-radio constraint-validation control.
checks: Confirm Matte coated is initially selected and its 170 gsm value appears in the local status.
Select Uncoated offset and verify the status updates to 120 gsm and the radio selection follows.
Confirm Recycled blend test is disabled, its reason is shown, and it cannot become selected.
Use arrow keys to move between enabled cards and inspect the hidden form value after selection.
guidelines: Use radio cards when choices need a short description or metadata in addition to a label.
State why an option is unavailable and keep the selected summary tied to the same value submitted by the form.

phone-input.summary: Shows the native country-aware phone entry with Argentina selected by default and an explicitly empty initial value.
demonstrates: The field begins empty and offers Argentina, Chile, and Brazil as suggested countries.
The helper text and local status describe formatting preview only; the scene does not place a call or claim that a number is verified.
The component provides country-aware entry and formatting while built-in validation messaging is disabled for this example.
limits: No phone number, person, workshop contact, or real contact route is represented.
Formatting does not establish that a number is assigned, reachable, or valid for service.
checks: Confirm the initial field is empty, Argentina is selected, and no example number is prefilled.
Type and clear a sample value; verify the local status switches between formatting preview and no number entered.
Confirm the explanation makes no verification or call claim.
guidelines: Use a phone input when country-aware number entry and formatting are part of the task.
Describe formatting separately from verification, assignment, reachability, or delivery.

money-input.summary: Edits a fictional Argentine-peso paper-and-ink allocation and locally calculates the remaining amount from a sample worksheet budget.
demonstrates: The sample worksheet budget is ARS 500,000; the initial allocation is ARS 125,000, leaving ARS 375,000.
The native money input is restricted to ARS, and its minor-unit scale follows the currency fraction digits reported by Intl.NumberFormat.
The remaining amount is calculated locally from the entered allocation and sample budget.
limits: All amounts are fictional planning figures, not an offer, quote, invoice, or current market price.
The arithmetic does not save, submit, or reconcile values with an external service.
checks: Confirm the initial allocation plus remaining amount equals the ARS 500,000 worksheet budget.
Edit the amount and use a quick-add chip; verify the remaining amount changes by the same amount.
Confirm ARS formatting matches the worksheet locale and the single-currency setting hides the currency chooser.
guidelines: Use a money input for amounts whose currency and locale-aware formatting matter.
State the currency and calculation context, and keep sample planning figures distinct from commercial offers.

color-picker.summary: Edit a sample ink color against warm paper and compare three original ink swatches with the selected hexadecimal readout.
demonstrates: The original sample inks are deep ink #202020, river blue #176B87, and poster vermilion #B8472D.
The selected color is reported as hex; the picker calculates a digital text-contrast ratio and threshold grade against #F4EBDD paper.
The picker supports editing the color and managing its swatches locally.
limits: These sample colors are not a product palette, ink specification, or proof of printed appearance.
The displayed grade assesses this digital text/background pair, not full interface accessibility or printed output.
checks: Confirm the three sample swatches and their hex values match the visible swatch labels.
Change the color and verify the selected hexadecimal readout follows the picker value.
Confirm the picker receives the warm paper background for its contrast readout.
guidelines: Use a color picker when users need to edit a color and inspect its value directly.
Name the comparison background and distinguish digital contrast readings from print behavior or compliance claims.

range-histogram-slider.summary: Filters a Córdoba sample worksheet of absolute trim-mark deviations and reports the number of observations in the selected interval.
demonstrates: The 20 original sample values are in millimetres and range from 0.05 to 0.62 mm.
The initial interval is 0.10–0.40 mm and contains 13 of the 20 observations, including both interval endpoints.
The two ARIA slider thumbs update the local count as their bounds move; the histogram bins summarize the sample distribution.
limits: These are illustrative worksheet observations, not calibration records or production measurements.
The selected interval is a descriptive filter and does not define a tolerance or acceptable production range.
checks: Confirm there are 20 nonnegative values and that 13 lie inclusively between 0.10 and 0.40 mm.
Move both thumbs and verify the displayed count matches the values within the selected interval.
Confirm the visible and spoken range values include the mm unit.
guidelines: Use a range histogram to select an interval from a one-dimensional sample and show the resulting count.
Name the measured quantity and unit, and distinguish a sample filter from an acceptance rule.

scrub-input.summary: Adjusts a sample per-edge trim allowance and calculates the resulting usable width of a 320 mm sheet.
demonstrates: The allowance starts at 3 mm per edge, so the displayed usable width is 314 mm.
The calculation is 320 mm minus twice the selected per-edge allowance; the control supports 0–12 mm with 0.5 mm steps and finer or coarser adjustments.
The native scrub field supports direct entry and expression input as well as label scrubbing.
limits: The dimensions are a sample planning calculation, not a machine setup or production specification.
The example assumes the same allowance on both edges and does not account for other sheet constraints.
checks: Confirm the initial arithmetic gives 320 − 2 × 3 = 314 mm.
Change the value and verify the result updates to 320 − 2 × allowance, retaining one decimal place.
Use the control reset and verify it returns to 3 mm.
guidelines: Use a scrub number field for a bounded numeric parameter that benefits from both direct typing and fine adjustment.
State the unit, bounds, and calculation affected by the parameter.

usage-meter.previewTitle: Paper used in the sample print week
usage-meter.summary: Breaks a fictional 16 kg paper allocation into three sample print-week categories and shows their total against the limit.
demonstrates: Text stock is 6.4 kg, cover stock is 3.2 kg, and proof sheets are 2.1 kg; together they use 11.7 kg of the 16 kg allocation.
The remaining unassigned amount is 4.3 kg, and the meter displays the separate segment amounts against the shared limit.
The values are fixed sample data; this scene does not imply inventory synchronization.
limits: The quantities are illustrative worksheet values, not a live scale reading or verified inventory.
The 16 kg limit is a sample allocation, not a safety or production threshold.
checks: Confirm the segment values sum to 11.7 kg and the unassigned amount is 4.3 kg.
Confirm the meter uses the same kilogram unit and 16 kg limit for all segments.
Inspect the segment labels and identify each portion without relying on color alone.
guidelines: Use a usage meter to show parts of a measured allowance and how they compare with a fixed limit.
Keep segment units consistent and label each component of the total.

onboarding-checklist.summary: Tracks four manually checked preparation steps for a fictional 16-page booklet, with paper stock already marked complete.
demonstrates: The checklist starts with paper stock complete and three remaining tasks: plate separations, proof review, and folding/counting.
Steps have no action callbacks, so checking them updates only the checklist's local state.
The completed title appears when all four sample steps are checked.
limits: The booklet and setup are illustrative; no production task or external workflow is started.
A checked item records a local example state and does not verify that work was performed.
checks: Confirm exactly four steps appear and the paper-stock step is initially complete.
Check and uncheck steps; verify the checklist progress changes and state remains local.
Complete all four steps and inspect the done title, then reopen a completed step if the component allows it.
guidelines: Use a checklist for a short set of tasks that people can complete in any order.
Describe local completion as a record of interaction unless an external task system confirms the work.

timeline.summary: Presents four fixed, fictional worksheet entries from a booklet exercise in reverse chronological order using Argentina time.
demonstrates: The sample entries on September 18, 2026 record paper stock, two plate separations, a trim mark, and a folded sample count of 24 copies.
The feed receives explicit event timestamps, a fixed reference time, and the America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires time zone.
The paper-stock entry is expanded by default; entries with detail can be expanded in place with the native timeline interaction.
limits: The timeline is static sample worksheet content, not a live or audited activity feed.
Its dates and details do not document a real person, workshop, or production run.
checks: Confirm four events appear newest first on September 18, 2026 and the fixed reference time follows them.
Expand and collapse event details and verify the details match their corresponding worksheet entry.
Confirm the time zone is America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires and no event uses an actor or portrait.
guidelines: Use a timeline when order and recency matter more than sorting or comparing values.
Supply stable event identities, explicit timestamps, a reference time, and the intended time zone.

stepper.summary: Navigates four local stages of a fictional booklet workflow with the step indicator and owned Back/Continue buttons.
demonstrates: The four stages are cut stock, print plates, fold sheets, and count the bundle; the initial current stage is Print plates.
Back and Continue move the controlled current index within the four stages; the stepper can also select an already completed stage.
At index four the stepper announces the sample sequence completion and the Continue control is disabled.
limits: Changing stages is local navigation and does not execute or record any production work.
The sequence demonstrates a sample ordering and is not a required real-world process.
checks: Confirm the initial current stage is Print plates and Back is enabled while Continue advances one stage.
Move backward and forward through all four stages and verify the current label follows the selected index.
Advance to completion and confirm the final count is four and Continue is disabled.
guidelines: Use a stepper to show position in a known ordered process and provide navigation when returning to earlier steps is useful.
Drive the current index from the surrounding flow and distinguish step navigation from task execution.

countdown.summary: Counts down to a fixed illustrative handoff time of November 20, 2026 at 09:00 in Buenos Aires.
demonstrates: The target is November 20, 2026 at 09:00 in America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires.
The native countdown updates the displayed time units against the fixed target and replaces them with the specified completion label after the target passes.
The target date and local time zone are explicit rather than dependent on the viewer's device zone.
limits: The date is an illustrative example, not a real booking, event, shipment, or deadline.
The countdown uses the viewer's device clock; it does not synchronize with an authoritative time source.
checks: Confirm the target resolves to November 20, 2026 at 09:00 in America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires.
Inspect the displayed units as time passes and verify the completion label is configured for after the target.
Confirm the adjacent note identifies the target as illustrative.
guidelines: Use a countdown for a fixed moment people need to wait for, and provide an explicit zone for local wall time.
Identify whether the target is a sample or authoritative event and state any clock-source limitation.

password-strength.summary: Shows the native local password-strength estimate with its built-in length, letter-case, number, and symbol rules.
demonstrates: The controlled field starts empty and estimates strength as text is entered using the component's default rules.
The field uses autocomplete off and is labeled for a sample proof-station passphrase.
The adjacent note states that the estimate runs locally and is not a server policy check.
limits: A client-side strength estimate does not verify compliance with a server's policy, blocklist, or account requirements.
The sample is not an account creation flow; users are told not to enter a real account password.
checks: Confirm the field starts empty and the built-in strength meter and rule list appear as text is entered.
Try a short sample and a longer varied sample; verify the displayed estimate changes according to the built-in rules.
Confirm the explanation distinguishes the local estimate from server policy and discourages real credentials.
guidelines: Use a password-strength meter as immediate client-side guidance while someone creates a password.
State the rules and limits of the estimate, and do not present it as authoritative server validation.

hold-to-confirm.summary: Fills a local proof-confirmation control over 900 ms from rest, with release rewind and an explicit reset.
demonstrates: Starting from rest, a 900 ms hold marks the local sample approved. Releasing early rewinds the fill; repressing during rewind resumes its current progress.
The reset button returns the state to unmarked and is disabled until the hold completes.
The adjacent status states that the marked state belongs to this local example.
limits: The interaction does not approve or record a real production proof.
The hold confirms only the local state change; it does not contact another person or system.
checks: Press and release before 900 ms; verify the sample state remains unmarked.
After the fill returns to rest, hold for 900 ms; verify the controlled state changes and Reset becomes available.
Reset the sample and verify the control returns to its initial state.
guidelines: Use hold-to-confirm for a consequential action whose instruction and consequence are already clear on screen.
Keep the confirmed state owned by the surrounding flow when it needs to be reset or reflected elsewhere.

confirm-morph.summary: Confirms removal of one visible sample proof note and uses the component's Undo action to restore the exact note text.
demonstrates: The confirmation prompt names the exact note: “Vermilion registration mark sits 0.2 mm right of the sample guide.”
Confirm synchronously removes the note from local state; Undo synchronously restores the same note.
Both confirmation and result timeouts are disabled so the result remains until the user acts.
limits: The note is an illustrative sample and no production record is changed.
Confirm and Undo update only the scene's local list; there is no pending network or persistence state.
checks: Open the confirmation and verify the full note detail is visible before confirming.
Confirm removal and verify the empty-list message and persistent done face appear.
Choose Undo and verify the original note text returns to the list.
guidelines: Use an in-place confirmation for a consequential but reversible action when the affected item can be named clearly.
Make Undo restore the actual prior state and avoid implying persistence when the change is local.

shortcut-recorder.summary: Records and displays an optional keyboard chord in local scene state, initially empty.
demonstrates: The shortcut value starts as null and the recorder's reset value is also null.
The component reports a normalized chord through onValueChange, and the scene displays the current stored value or “none.”
The helper text says the chord is stored only in this example and does not bind a system shortcut or trigger an action.
limits: The chord is not persisted and is not registered with the operating system or another application.
The example does not demonstrate whether the recorded chord can be intercepted by the browser or system elsewhere.
checks: Confirm the initial value is none and reset restores none after recording a chord.
Record a chord and verify the displayed value matches the recorder's normalized value.
Confirm the helper text makes no OS binding or action-trigger claim.
guidelines: Use a shortcut recorder when users need to enter a chord and inspect the normalized combination.
State whether a chord is merely stored or actually registered and invoked by an application.

expanding-search.summary: Filters four original local booklet-manifest entries and displays the title and metadata of the selected result.
demonstrates: The manifest contains Edition 08 colophon, Black plate notes, Proof sheet 08-B, and Cover trim guide entries.
The native search uses item titles, groups, metadata, and keywords; selecting an item updates the visible selected-entry line.
The search offers the first two entries as initial suggestions and includes the component's built-in clear behavior.
limits: Search is limited to four hard-coded sample entries and does not query a catalog or service.
Selecting a result reports its details locally and does not navigate to a document.
checks: Search title, metadata and keyword terms; verify matching entries. Group headings organize results but are not searched.
Select a result and verify its actual title and metadata appear in the selected-entry line.
Use the built-in clear control; verify the query clears, the suggestions return, and the selected result remains unchanged.
guidelines: Use an expanding search in a compact region where a full-time field would take space.
Make clear whether result selection opens content, navigates, or only reports a selection.

file-dropzone.summary: Checks up to two locally selected SVG or PNG files, flags sizes over 64 KB, and reports their actual names without uploading.
demonstrates: The dropzone accepts image/svg+xml and image/png and permits two rows. Matching files over 64 KB remain as failed rows and consume a slot.
onFilesChange updates a local readout with the actual selected file count and names; no default files are preloaded.
No onUpload is provided: valid files are local selections; oversize files show size errors and remain in the file readout until removed.
limits: The example does not upload files, send them to a server, or save them beyond the current browser session.
Selection and file type/size checks do not validate the artwork's content or production readiness.
checks: Confirm the initial count is zero and no file rows are preloaded.
Select one or two accepted files within the size limit and verify the count and names update.
Try an unsupported MIME type and verify rejection; select an oversize supported file and verify its failed row and count, remove it, then verify a third-file limit.
guidelines: Use a dropzone when local drag-and-drop or file selection is useful, and state accepted types, count, and size limits.
Distinguish selecting files from uploading, processing, or validating their contents.

reactions.summary: Shows three fictional acknowledgment tallies and toggles the viewer's own local reaction with the native reaction control.
demonstrates: The original options are Registration clear, Proof readable, and Fold sequence ready, with initial sample counts of 3, 2, and 1.
The controlled value receives each actual reaction change, including the selected reaction's count and reacted state.
The reset button restores the three original counts and clears the local reacted state.
limits: Initial counts are fictional sample tallies and are not attributed to people or a shared service.
Reaction changes exist only in local component state and are not saved or broadcast.
checks: Confirm the three initial sample counts are 3, 2, and 1 and all begin unreacted.
Toggle each existing reaction and add one through the native picker; verify counts and reacted state update.
Use Reset counts and verify the original options, counts, and unreacted states return.
guidelines: Use reactions for quick acknowledgments with a small fixed set of meanings.
Label what each reaction means and state whether displayed counts are shared, sourced, or sample values.

demonstrates: Reveals the new page theme from the button center.
The actual host theme changes in both directions; the same original Rosario booklet proof and its data remain unchanged.
The button state and current-mode readout follow the host theme provider. The variants differ only in whole-page transition geometry.

Whole-page movement requires the theme-transition bridge and its CSS. Unsupported browsers and reduced motion apply the theme immediately.

guidelines: Choose one transition style for the same action throughout the application.
Keep page data unchanged when switching viewing mode; use the host theme state rather than independent state per preview.

stats-band.summary: Shows three finite figures from a fictional 16-page print worksheet, with a copy-count trend and a trim-offset distribution.
demonstrates: The six sample edition counts are 120, 144, 168, 192, 216, and 240 copies; the trend ends at 240 for Edition 08.
The worksheet plans 960 sheets as 240 copies × 4 imposed sheets per copy.
Ten trim-offset samples in millimetres have a median of 0.215 mm and a range of 0.08–0.38 mm; the distribution visual bins those same ten values across 0–0.50 mm.
limits: All values are illustrative worksheet data, not audited production records or live measurements.
The trim-offset summary is descriptive and does not define a tolerance or acceptable print range.
The small visuals summarize only the supplied values and are not an external feed.
checks: Confirm the trend contains six ascending sample-run values and ends at the displayed 240-copy total.
Verify 240 × 4 = 960 planned sheets and that the stated unit is sheets.
Recompute the median of the ten trim samples as (0.20 + 0.23) / 2 = 0.215 mm; confirm the histogram bins sum to ten and span a 0–0.50 mm domain.
Switch between Divided and Plain layouts and confirm the figures and context values remain the same.
guidelines: Use a stats band for a small set of headline measures with short context and, when useful, a compact visual summary.
Keep visual data tied to the displayed quantity, label its unit and domain, and distinguish sample summaries from thresholds or verified records.

animated-counter.previewTitle: Copy count for the selected sample edition
animated-counter.summary: Formats and animates a sample booklet copy count while edition selection and a bounded local adjustment update the displayed total.
demonstrates: The edition selector starts at Edition 08 and offers Edition 03–08 baseline counts of 480, 600, 720, 840, 960, and 1,080 copies.
The counter uses an edition label naming copies, English number formatting, zero decimal places, and animate-on-view behavior.
Add 24 increases the local worksheet display by 24, up to a 120-copy adjustment; changing edition resets the adjustment and Reset total restores the selected baseline.
limits: Counts and adjustments are illustrative sample worksheet values, not recorded or produced copy quantities.
The controls update local state only; they do not submit a print job or persist the count.
checks: Confirm Edition 08 initially shows 1,080 with grouped English digits and no fractional digits. The edition label and worksheet baseline name copies.
Select each edition and verify the displayed baseline matches its listed count.
Add 24 repeatedly; verify the value rises by 24 each time and stops at a 120-copy adjustment.
Reset after an adjustment and verify the selected edition's baseline returns; choose another edition and confirm its adjustment starts at zero.
guidelines: Use an animated counter when the changing numeric value is the focus and the displayed unit is explicit.
Keep number formatting and labels stable while values change, and distinguish local sample adjustments from recorded totals.

otp-input.summary: Enter the six-digit code for a fictional Rosario worksheet; a complete match selects that worksheet locally.
guidelines: Type 731408 to select the worksheet; a different complete code shows an associated error.
Clear resets the controlled value; no authentication service is connected.
limits: No authentication service or actual one-time-code delivery.
Paste and browser autofill depend on the browser and the input integration.
checks: Type matching and nonmatching codes; inspect the result, help and error associations.
Move with arrow keys and Backspace; clear and resize.

swipe-actions.summary: Mark three fictional print proofs checked without removing them, or archive them through each row’s actions.
guidelines: Use the More actions menu as the keyboard alternative to the swipe gesture.
Mark checked retains the row; Archive proof removes it and records its title. Restore returns all three.
limits: Archive updates local preview state. Connect a service in the consuming app and test touch gestures on target devices.
checks: Mark and unmark a proof; archive the first, middle and last row using keyboard menus.
Inspect focus and the empty state, then restore all proofs.

card-stack.summary: Review three original geometric cover studies for a fictional Córdoba booklet, with Keep, Pass, Undo and Start over.
guidelines: Use the decision buttons or focus the stack and press Left/Right.
Undo reverses the last decision; Start over resets the deck and kept-study list.
limits: The shortlist remains local; no publication or purchase occurs. Test dragging and keyboard navigation in the consuming layout.
checks: Keep and pass all three studies, undo and reset; inspect the visible result after each action.
Inspect narrow/enlarged layouts and a live change to reduced motion.

expandable-card.summary: Expands a sample Edition 12 trim-and-fold card to show its paper plan and a reversible local review mark.
demonstrates: The card starts collapsed with an 8-page, 360-copy sample broadside summary and expands from a 340 px cap toward 560 px, bounded by its container.
The expanded content describes two imposed sheets per copy, a 4 mm outer margin, 120 gsm uncoated paper, and black and river-blue plates.
The nested action toggles a local worksheet review mark; the card's own trigger and Escape key provide expand/collapse behavior.
limits: The worksheet and review mark are sample content and are not saved or certified as a production print sheet.
checks: Open and close the card with its trigger and confirm the same details are revealed and hidden.
Expand the card and verify its width grows only within the preview container; press Escape and confirm focus returns to its trigger.
Toggle the local review mark and confirm its status changes independently of card expansion.
guidelines: Use an expandable card when a short summary needs more detail without navigating away.
Keep the collapsed title and description useful, and give nested actions their own distinct outcome.

bottom-sheet.summary: Opens a two-detent sheet for selecting one sample ink plate and adding or removing it from a local review note.
demonstrates: The trigger opens the sheet at the 46% viewport detent; the grabber and native sheet interaction can move it to the 90% detent or close it.
The owned Select chooses Black or River blue and updates the visible plate description.
The action toggles the selected plate in local review-note state, while the parent line reflects open, peek, expanded, or closed state.
limits: Plate names and note are illustrative local state; no production worksheet is updated or saved.
checks: Open the sheet and verify it starts at the lower detent; expand and collapse it with the grabber, then close it.
Select each plate and verify its description changes; add and remove it from the local note and verify the status follows.
Close and reopen the sheet; confirm the sheet starts at the lower detent and the local plate selection remains explicit.
guidelines: Use a bottom sheet for a secondary task that benefits from a peek state and can expand into more content.
Set detents to meaningful heights and identify local selection separately from submitted or persisted work.

user-menu.summary: Shows the native account menu with a generic local identity, controlled presence and theme preferences, three local destinations, and a local close/reopen outcome.
demonstrates: The menu has no portrait and uses the reserved example address editor@example.invalid.
Presence and theme choices update controlled local state. The selected theme also changes the contained paper specimen; System follows the operating-system color preference.
Paper ledger, Plate notes, and Edition colophon open distinct sample content panels. Sign out closes the local preview and exposes a Reopen print-room menu button.
limits: The identity and menu content are fictional sample values, not a person, organization, or external account.
No account service is connected: sign out closes only the local menu preview. Theme selection affects only its paper specimen, not the host page.
checks: Open the menu and select each destination; verify the ledger, plate notes, and colophon panels show their corresponding sample details.
Change presence and theme preferences; verify the paper specimen changes between light and dark, and System follows the operating-system preference without changing the host page.
Choose Sign out and verify focus moves to Reopen print-room menu after the original trigger is removed; reopen the menu and confirm the local preview returns.
guidelines: Use an account menu for a small group of account destinations and inline preferences, with a clear local outcome for each item.
Treat status, theme, destinations, and sign out as local preview state unless an account service is connected.

chat-thread.summary: Shows a local print-room exchange about Edition 08 stock, ink plates, and cover trim, with the native message composer and reactions.
demonstrates: Three desk labels exchange specific notes for a 32-page, 180-copy sample edition printed on 120 gsm uncoated stock.
The built-in composer appends a new local message; the reaction picker toggles the selected emoji and count.
The thread uses its native scroll area and sent/read message states; attachments are disabled for this text-only sample.
limits: Desk labels and messages are fictional sample content, not people or an actual print-room conversation.
Messages and reactions are held by the component for this preview only; no network, attachment, or delivery service is connected.
checks: Send a short proof note and confirm it appears as a new local message with the current editor as author.
Toggle the existing check reaction and confirm its count and pressed state update; toggle again to remove the local reaction.
guidelines: Use a chat thread for short sequential updates that benefit from a composer and message-level reactions.
Keep participant identities and delivery states tied to actual data when connecting a service; this scene uses desk labels and local state.

comment-thread.summary: Shows threaded annotations for an Edition 08 booklet proof, including a nested margin note and native comment actions.
demonstrates: The sample data records four 8-page signatures, 120 gsm uncoated stock, a 4 mm fold and trim margin, and two named ink plates.
The native composer adds top-level comments or replies; reactions toggle, and the local editor can edit or delete their own comment.
Resolve folds the thread into its summary chip; reopen restores the comments. Mention suggestions use the three supplied desk labels.
limits: Desk labels and proof notes are fictional sample content, not people or an actual production approval.
Comments, reactions, edits, and resolution remain in component-local state and are not saved to a service.
checks: Reply to a note and confirm the reply nests beneath the selected comment; add a top-level comment and confirm the count updates.
Toggle a reaction, edit the local editor's own note, and delete it with the confirmation action.
Resolve and reopen the thread; confirm the sample comments remain available after reopening.
guidelines: Use a comment thread for review notes that need replies, ownership, and a resolved state.
Keep author permissions and persistence in the host application when connecting real review data.

hero-section.previewTitle: A folio planned from the fold
hero-section.summary: Introduces the Folio 21 booklet in the component's content-height editorial layout.
demonstrates: The scene uses the minimal editorial layout and an original SVG signature diagram.
The original brief gives the Folio 21 sample's 24-page extent, three 8-page signatures, 140-copy quantity, and 100 gsm text stock.
Sheet plan reveals the corresponding three-signature and two-plate cover details in local page content.
limits: Folio 21 is fictional sample print data; the hero action reveals a local note and does not create a production order.
The hero content uses no supplied portraits, external image, or external destination.
checks: Verify the editorial heading and folio brief; reveal the sheet plan and inspect its signature diagram.
Activate Sheet plan and verify the three-signature count, plate colors, and 5 mm trim note appear; activate it again to hide the note.
guidelines: Use the minimal layout for a content-height editorial opening that follows its copy and visual.
Give preview actions a local content result or a meaningful destination.

faq-section.summary: Answers practical questions about signatures, stock, plate colors, trim, and the sample edition quantity, with three selectable FAQ layouts.
demonstrates: The owned Select switches the component among accordion, topic-column, and searchable layouts using the same five original questions.
The answers preserve the sample data: three 8-page signatures, 100 gsm text stock, 220 gsm cover stock, two cover plates, a 5 mm inner rule, and 140 sample copies.
The native accordion/search/category controls operate on the supplied question data; the contact path is hidden.
limits: The specifications describe a fictional print sample and are not a production instruction or order.
checks: Switch between all three layouts and verify the same five questions remain available.
Open multiple answers in accordion mode; switch to topic columns and confirm the categories filter their questions; search for 5 mm in search mode and confirm the trim answer appears.
guidelines: Choose accordion for one sequence of questions, columns for category-led browsing, and search when readers need to locate a term.
Keep answers aligned with the edition's source worksheet and do not turn sample values into production promises.

blog-grid.summary: Presents a fictional Argentine print journal with original text articles on imposition, paper, ink, proofing, and edition quantities.
demonstrates: Seven text-only articles provide a featured entry, five category filters, multi-page results, dates, reading times, and complete in-place article bodies.
The authored notes share consistent Folio 21 values: 24 pages, three 8-page signatures, 100 gsm text stock, 220 gsm cover stock, two named plates, a 5 mm margin, and 140 sample copies.
The component's category filter, pagination, article reader, and return-to-grid behavior operate on the supplied original records.
limits: The journal, archive labels, and print worksheet are fictional sample content; no author portraits or external image assets are used.
The article reader is local preview state and does not navigate to or save a remote article.
checks: Filter by Paper and Ink and verify only matching article cards remain; choose All to restore the full collection.
Advance through the pages, open a card in the reader, then close it and confirm the list context returns.
guidelines: Use featured content for the lead article and keep category labels consistent with each record.
Supply stable IDs, ISO dates, useful excerpts, and body paragraphs when the in-place reader is enabled.

comparison-table.summary: Compares a two-plate booklet specification, a black-only proof, and a folded dummy using one consistent sample worksheet.
demonstrates: All columns preserve 24 pages and three 8-page signatures; text and cover stock values distinguish the printed editions from the lighter dummy.
The two-plate version includes black text and an oxide-red cover rule 5 mm inside trim; the black-only proof and folded dummy omit the oxide-red plate.
The native difference switch filters identical rows, the narrow layout lets readers select a comparison column, and the highlighted-column action records a visible local worksheet selection.
limits: These are fictional sample specifications, not a comparison of commercial printers or a quote. The 5 mm oxide-red-rule margin applies only to the two-plate cover.
The selection action changes only local page state; it does not submit or order a print run.
checks: Turn on Only differences and verify the equal page-count and signature rows disappear while differing stock, plate, and quantity rows remain.
At a narrow width, choose each comparison column and verify it appears beside the highlighted two-plate specification.
Activate Use the two-plate spec and verify the worksheet selection names the two-plate version and its 140-copy sample quantity.
guidelines: Keep every row keyed to the same column IDs and use explicit notes where a value needs qualification.
Use a highlighted column for the intended reference spec and describe example values as samples rather than market claims.

file-upload.summary: Select, validate, and remove local proof files for a fictional Folio 21 print review without presenting a transfer or saved upload.
demonstrates: Choose or drop SVG and plain-text files; the FileUpload component validates accepted extensions and the 32 KB maximum, and exposes its built-in per-file removal control.
Create local SVG plate and trim-checklist File objects with valid SVG or plain-text content, then see their names and sizes in the selected-file list.
Clear the controlled selection and confirm the selected-file count returns to zero.
limits: No onUpload callback is supplied: the component reports selected files only and does not transmit, persist, or complete a server upload.
The sample assets are generated in browser memory and are illustrative print-review files, not production proofs or verified press specifications.
checks: Create one plate SVG and one trim checklist; verify each appears in the selected list and the live count reports two files.
Remove either file with its built-in remove control and verify the remaining file and count update; clear the selection and confirm the empty state.
Select a file with an unsupported extension or larger than 32 KB and verify the component marks it for attention while leaving it removable.
guidelines: Use file selection for local review when no transfer service is connected, and describe selection separately from upload completion.
State accepted formats and size limits near the control, and keep rejected files removable so people can recover without restarting the selection.

contact-section.summary: Capture a local print-review note, browse paper/proof/fold references, or compare three fictional desks with actual local clocks.
demonstrates: Validate name, email, and a message of at least 20 characters; capture the trimmed payload in the local review list.
Switch form, reference-desk, and office-clock layouts with a Select while keeping the form draft.
Move between reference desks with arrow/Home/End keys and copy actual reference strings.
limits: The preview records notes in component state only. It does not send messages or promise a response.
The desks and opening hours are fictional; the named cities use real IANA time zones.
checks: Try an empty form and a short message; verify errors name the affected fields and focus the first invalid input.
Write a valid note, change layouts and return, then capture it and write another note.
Change reference tabs by keyboard, inspect each detail, and compare the live office clocks.
guidelines: Keep processing in onSubmit; reject to preserve entries and expose a retryable error.
Use channel details for real contact actions or references, and distinguish illustrative offices from actual service availability.

newsletter-signup.summary: Validate and keep a local reader address while previewing an original Folio 21 issue stack in inline and card layouts.
demonstrates: Choose inline or card layout with the same Select used elsewhere.
Capture a valid trimmed email in a visible local list; the next sample issue is addressed to that email.
Use a different email to reset the form and return focus to its input.
limits: The preview has no mailing service, tracking, or subscription persistence. It does not claim delivery.
Sample issue dates, subjects, and geometric thumbnails are original illustrative content.
checks: Submit an empty or malformed address, then a valid address; verify the list and addressed issue agree.
Switch layouts, confirm the captured state is retained, and reset to enter another address.
guidelines: Provide onSubscribe to connect a processor and reject to keep the entered email on failure.
Keep issue data and privacy text specific to the actual publication and service.

cta-section.summary: Compare centered, split, and dismissible-banner callouts whose actions add actual local proof and paper notes.
demonstrates: Use a Select to choose centered, split, or banner layout.
Add proof or paper notes to the visible local worksheet with distinct primary and secondary actions.
Dismiss the banner and restore it with keyboard focus transferred only from the removed control.
limits: Actions update local component state; no remote booking, account, or proof request is created.
The split illustration is a static original print worksheet, not a simulated provisioning workflow.
checks: Activate both note actions and verify each note is added to the worksheet.
Choose Banner, dismiss it with the keyboard, restore it, and verify focus remains usable.
Resize the callout and enlarge text; keep labels and the Dismiss action complete.
guidelines: Use href for real navigation, onClick for real actions, or an explicit confirmedLabel for a local toggle.
The host owns focus after removal; the supplied preview block handles dismissal and restore as one owner.

site-header.summary: Browse a bounded Folio21 archive page with mega, simple, or centered navigation.
demonstrates: Select three distinct header layouts; open grouped destinations in the mega menu.
Choose a destination to show its actual print note and current section.
Scroll the framed page and use the narrow menu without losing its actions.
limits: Destinations select local sample content; no external site is opened.
The menu is a navigation disclosure, not a modal dialog.
checks: Open a mega panel with Arrow Down, select a link, and close with Escape.
Use the narrow menu and its grouped links; resize to the desktop layout.
Scroll the bounded page and inspect the solid header background.
guidelines: Use href for real links and onNavigate for locally handled destinations.
Supply scrollContainer when the header belongs to a nested scroller.

public-header.summary: Use document-fixed navigation with theme-aware glass activated by scroll or the mobile menu.
demonstrates: Scroll past eight pixels to activate the glass material in the current theme.
Open mobile navigation, choose a local page, and return to its toggle with Escape.
limits: The fixed header is isolated in a catalog viewport; the installable example occupies its own document.
Navigation changes local sample content; it does not contact the source website.
checks: Switch light and dark themes with the header scrolled and check navigation legibility.
Open the mobile menu by keyboard, choose a page, and verify the current link.
Close with Escape and resize to desktop while the menu is open.
guidelines: Use this header at document level, with enough top space for its four-rem bar.
Reuse GlassHeaderLayer inside a positioned rams-public-glass-scope.
Apply the RAMS dark class to the theme ancestor so the tint and foreground follow the current theme.

site-footer.summary: Compare link columns, a minimal footer row, and a closing wordmark with original Folio21 reference notes.
demonstrates: Use a Select to change among three footer layouts.
Select a print reference to read its actual note.
Validate an email and keep it in the visible local list.
limits: The newsletter captures local state only; no mailing service or delivery is claimed.
The closing wordmark is a decorative repeated brand name with an intentional lower-edge fade.
checks: Select each layout and activate a reference link.
Submit an empty or malformed email, then a valid email; verify the address in the list.
Enlarge text and inspect the newsletter controls and link columns.
guidelines: Provide onSubscribe for actual processing; rejection keeps the address available for retry.
Supply meaningful href values or onNavigate; destinations without either remain passive text.

plan-comparison.summary: Compare two A3 print methods, their actual sample ARS totals, and the input sheets needed for 100 or 500 finished sheets.
demonstrates: Select 100 or 500 finished sheets and compare the changed figures.
Filter eight production specifications to their five differences.
Choose or clear one method and read the actual spare/input-sheet allocation.
limits: Figures are illustrative worksheet data, not a supplier quote, purchase or payment.
checks: Switch allocations, verify both totals and select/clear each method.
Enable differences only and verify five of eight specifications.
Keep numeric values, method labels and selection controls readable at narrow widths and enlarged text.
guidelines: Compare the same finished quantity and currency for every method.
Keep each specification associated with its method after narrow reflow.

changelog-feed.summary: Browse fourteen original print-production notes by kind and month, inspect their real code payloads, and export the visible record.
demonstrates: Filter New, Improved and Fixed entries, alone or in combination.
Jump to a month and expand actual trim, fold and sheet-count details.
Copy a code payload or download the filtered record as Markdown.
limits: Dates, versions and revisions belong to the illustrative Folio21 print record.
Export dispatch does not prove a file was saved; image binaries are not embedded in Markdown.
checks: Check kind counts, combine and clear filters, then jump among visible months.
Expand the five code entries and inspect their copied payloads.
Download a filtered record and inspect its exact entries and line breaks.
guidelines: Keep entries keyed to the supplied months and supply useful details.
Keep literal code scrollable locally and preserve the full copy/export payload.

page-header.summary: Manage local print checks, count snapshots, notes and downloadable job files in a header that condenses as its body scrolls.
demonstrates: Complete, add and reset actual local checks with matching progress and counts.
Record a snapshot of current counts, switch tabs and inspect actual notes.
Download original job files and copy the current page address.
limits: Changes stay in the mounted worksheet; no remote project or service is updated.
Production benches use abstract initials rather than invented people or portraits.
checks: Scroll the body, inspect condensed and expanded headers, then switch all tabs.
Complete the first, middle and final open checks and keep focus usable; reset.
Download the four files and inspect their bytes; record a snapshot and copy the actual page link.
guidelines: Keep counts and local business changes immediate, independent of animation.
Retire outgoing panels and controls before their exit paint finishes.

signup-form.summary: Validate reader details and keep the submitted name, address and edition-notes choice in the local Folio21 register.
demonstrates: Validate required name, email and password fields and inspect password feedback.
Submit valid details through the actual callback and read the non-secret local record.
Reset and recover from a duplicate-address callback error without losing entries.
limits: The callback receives the password, but the example list stores only name, email and edition-notes choice.
No account, provider identity or mailing subscription is created by this local record.
checks: Submit empty/malformed fields, then valid details and verify the list.
Reset, enter the same address and verify the real callback error preserves fields.
Exercise a deferred caller and connected provider handler without claiming authentication.
guidelines: Connect real processing through onSubmit and reject to expose a recoverable error.
Provider choices appear only when onProvider is supplied; that handler owns any actual navigation.

sign-in.summary: Compare a local reader code or record a method choice for the entered address at the Rosario reading table.
demonstrates: Validate the address and apply a real typo-domain suggestion when available.
Compare six local digits, recover from a mismatch and restart immediately.
Keep the entered address and chosen method in a visible local visit list.
limits: This is a UI state machine with local code comparison, not authentication or identity verification.
Provider and passkey choices record a selected method; no provider or device service is contacted.
checks: Use invalid/valid addresses, compare wrong/correct codes and restart.
Record code, passkey and provider choices and verify actual callback payloads.
Reset and verify focus and address editing remain usable.
guidelines: Treat onSignIn as a local notification, not proof of identity.
Enforce any real access control in the consuming application and its services.

login-centered.summary: Switch between new and returning readers, compare a local code, and record the address, method and visit mode for the Córdoba reading room.
demonstrates: Record the explicit illustrative address and selected method, or compare a code for an entered address.
Switch new/returning reader modes and preserve the chosen mode in callback data.
Open native disclosures for local reader terms and privacy information.
limits: Fixed local comparison codes and method choices do not authenticate a person or verify a passkey.
Records live only in this mounted page; no remote account or email delivery exists.
checks: Switch modes, compare wrong/correct codes, restart and recover.
Record passkey/provider choices and verify address, method and mode.
Open and close both legal disclosures with keyboard and inspect focus and enlarged layout.
guidelines: Supply a real demoEmail only for a clearly illustrative record; never infer an authenticated identity.
Use real terms/privacy destinations in a consuming app and keep security enforcement outside this example.

morph-select.summary: Choose a sample La Plata, Rosario or Córdoba stock to calculate the mass of one hundred A3 sheets.
demonstrates: The controlled selection contains ten stocks in three groups, with grammage metadata and one unavailable choice.
The selected grammage calculates the estimated paper mass from the fixed 297 × 420 mm sheet dimensions.
Automatic search filters stock labels and location keywords; Clear stock restores the empty allocation.
limits: Stocks and locations are fictional worksheet data, not supplier inventory or a quotation.
The calculation includes paper only; ink, packing and production waste are excluded.
checks: Search Rosario, choose Neutral white and verify 160 gsm and 1.996 kg for 100 sheets.
Use arrow keys and Enter, then reopen and press Escape; inspect selection and focus return.
Confirm Heavy ivory is unavailable and cannot become selected.
Clear the stock and choose again; inspect grouped labels, metadata and natural wrapping at enlarged text.
guidelines: Keep supplementary choice metadata beside the option it describes.
Show the downstream allocation calculated from the selected stock.
